question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (Haritakyadi Varga, Chapter 1, verse 147):

दार्वीभेदाऽऽम्रन्या च सुरभीदारुदारु च । कर्पूरा प्रचपत्रा स्यात्मुरीमत्सुरतारका ।।१९८।। आम्रगंधिहरिद्रा या सा शीता वातला मता । पित्तहन्मधुरा तिक्ता सर्वकण्डूविनाशनी ।।१९९।।
answer_text: Latin: Curcuma amada Roxb. Fam: Zingiberaceae Hin: Aamiyahaladi Eng: Mango ginger Paryāyanāma (Synonyms): Dārvībhēdā, Āmaragandhā, Surbabihī, Dārudāru, Karpūra, Padmapatrā, Surīmaṭ and Suratārakā. It is Śitavīrya (Cold in potency), Increses Vāta doṣa, Subsides Pitta doṣa, Madhurā (Sweet) and Tiktā (Bitter) in taste, it cures all types Kaṇḍū (Itching). Utpattisthāna (Natural territory): It is distributed throughout India. Especialy in Bengal and Konkan regions. Swarūpa (Botanical description): It is a tuberous herb reaches upto 2-3 ft. in height. Leaves 30-45 cm.long and 7.5-12 cm. wide, oblong - lanceolate, petioles long, more, pale green, narrow at the base and apex. Flowers as arranged in spikes, elongated as t the bracts, whitish or pale yellow in colour. Prayojya anga (Part used): Mūla- Rhizome. Chemical constituents: Essential oils, Gums, Sugars, Resins, Starch, Albuminoids, Organic acids etc
citation: Bhavaprakasha Nighantu — Haritakyadi Varga, Chapter 1, verse 147
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Haritakyadi Varga, Chapter 1, verse 147.

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (Karpuradi Varga, Chapter 2, verse 204):

अगुरु प्रवरं लोहं राजाहँ योगजं तथा । वंशिकं कृमिजं वाऽपि कृमिजग्धमनार्यकम् ।।२१।। अगुरूष्णं कटु त्वच्यं तिक्त तीक्ष्णञ्व पित्तलम् । लघु कर्णाक्षिरोगघ्नं शीतवातकफप्रणुत् ।।२२।। कृष्णा गुणाधिकं तत्तु लोहवद्वारि मज्जति । अगुरुप्रभवः स्नेहः कृष्णागुरुसमः स्मृतः ।। २३ ।।
answer_text: Skin aliments: Decoction of wood and bark used in Twak rogas (Skin infections), Vrna (Wounds), etc. Mātrā (Dosage): Cūrṇa: 1-3gms. AGARU AND KRSNĀGURU Latin: Aquilaria agollacha Roxb. Fam: Thymeleaceae Eng: Eagle wood Hin: Agar, Kalaagar Paryāyanāma (Synonyms): Pravara, Loha, Rājārha, Yogaja, Vamśika, Kṛmija, Kṛmijagdha and Anāryaka. Guna karma (Properties and indications): Aguru is Usna virya (Hot in poten¬ cy), Kaṭu (Pungent), Twachya (Useful in skin conditions), Tikta (Bitter) in taste, Tīkṣna (Penetrating), Increases Pitta doşa and Laghu (Light for digestion). It cures Netra-Karna roga (Diseases of eyes and ears), Ŝitā (Relieves cold) and Diseases of Vāta and Kapha. Krşnāguru has more enanced in properties than Agaru, sinks in water like iron. An oil obtained from agaru is similar to that of Krşna āguru in properties and indications. Utpattisthāna (Natural territory): Found in eastern parts of India. Swarūpa (Botanical description): An evergreen large tree grows upto 20-23m in height. Leaves oppositely arranged 5-10 long and 2-5cm wide., acuminate apex, caudate base, glabrous, silky glossy, parallel nerved & short pedicle. Flowers are white colour arranged in short peduncled umbels. Fruit long slightly compressed, obovate, 3-5 cm long & wrinkled. Sap wood is soft, light weight, white- light yellow colour does not possess any specific odour. Heartwood available in cut pieces dark brown to nearly black, fracture hard, No characteristic smell & taste. Prayojya aṅga (Part used): Kāṇḍasāra (Heart wood), Qualities of good Agaru: Black in colour, Sticky or greasy in chew, It sinks when put in a water, and burns with bright flame leaves off pleasant odour. Chemical constituents: Essential oil which contains Selinene, Dihydroselinene

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (Karpuradi Varga, Chapter 2, verse 224):

जातीफलं जातिकोशं मालतीफलमित्यपि । जातिफलं रसे तिक्त तीक्ष्णोष्णं रोचन लघु । कट्टर्क दीपन ग्राहि स्वर्यं श्लेष्मानिलापहम् ।।५४११ निहन्ति मुखवैरस्यं मलदौर्गन्ध्यकृष्णताः कृमिकासवमिश्वासशोषपीनसहहहुजः १११५ ५११ जातीफलस्य त्वक् प्रोक्ता जातीपत्री भिषग्वरैः ।।५६।। जातीपत्री लघुः स्वादुः कटुष्णा रुचिवर्णकृत् । कफकासवमिश्वासतृष्णाकृमिविषापहा ।।५७।।
answer_text: Respiratory disease: It is good respiratory stimulant expectorant useful in Kāsa (cough) etc. diseases. In Swāsa (Dyspnoea), a medicated smoke of Shilarasa, Guggulu and Padmaka should be used. External uses: It is valuable remedy for skin diseases, mixed with Olive oil and apply locally in Dadru (Ringworm), Kanḍū (Itching), Pāmā (Scabies) etc. Mātrā (Dosage): 1-2 gms. JĀTĪPHALA Family: Myristicaceae Latin: Myristica fragrance Houtt. ng: Nutmeg Hin: Jayphala 18 JA-413 AVAPRAKĀŚA NIGHAN Paryāyanāma (Synonyms): Jātī Kośa and Mālatīphala. Guṇa karma (Properties and indications): Jatiphala is Tikta (Bitter), Tīkṣṇa (Penetrating), Uṣṇa vīrya (Hot in potency), Recana (Purgative), Laghu (Light for digestion), Kaṭu (Pungent) in taste, Dīpana (Appetizers), Grāhī (Absorbent) and Swarya (Good for voice). It cures diseases of Kapha and Vāta, Mukhadourgandya (Relieves bad breath), Maladourgandya (Relieves bad odour of faceas), Feacal discoloration, Kṛmi (Worm infestations), Kāsa (Cough), Chardi (Vomiting), Swāsa (Dyspnoea), Soṣa (Emaciation), Pīnasa (Running nose) and Hṛdya roga ( Cardiac Diseases). Note: Myristicin malbarica a source plant is a common adulterant and substitute. Utpattisthāna (Natural territory): It is a native of East Moluccas and cultivated in many parts if Southern India. Swarūpa (Botanical description): An everygreen tree with spreading branches grows upto 25 ft. Bark is greyish brown smooth. Leaves 2-5 inch long, elliptical-ovate, accuminate apex, obtuse base and pale under side. Flower are small pale yellow in color, usually single sexed in axillary racemose. Fruit ovid or pyriform, 1-2 inches across develop into yellow fleshy fruit, the ripen fruit splits to exposea. Seed single, purple brown nut, enclosed by an aril. Prayojya aṅga (Part used): Bīja (Seed), Koṣa- Jātīpatri. Chemical Constituents: Nutmeg has volatile oil contains Myristicin, Myristic acid, Engenol & Iso engenol it also contains Nutmeg butter, Fatty acids, Aromatic blasams, Starch and Fibrous substance etc. Digestive disease: The essential oil is Uttejaka (Stimulant) and Anulomaka (Carminative) and is administered in Atisāra (Diarrhoea), Pravahīkā (Dysentery) and Śūla (Abdominal pain). It’s Infusion is said to be useful in quenching the Tṛṣṇā (Thrist) of Visūcikā (Cholrea) patients. External uses: The extracted oil is used externally in various painful conditions like chronic Āmavāta (Rheumatism), Sandhiśūla (Joint inflammation), sprain, spasm, Dantasūla (Tooth ache ) etc., painful conditions. The oil prepared with seeds is applied to male genitals for promoting erectability. In case of Vipadika (Cracks in feet), a paste prepared from Jātiphala is applied externally. In Vyanga (Freckles), the paste of the aril of the Jātīphala applied externally. Mātrā (Dosage): Cūrṇa: 1-3 gms., Taila: 1 to 5 drops. JĀTĪPATRĪ Latin: Myristica fragrance Houtt. Fam: Myristicaceae Hin: Javitri ng: Mace The name jatiphala has very popular in Vedas. It is an unrippen seeds enclosed by fleshy red net like skin covering is called as aril or javitri. Guna karma (Properties and indications): It is Laghu (Light for digestion), Madhura (Sweet) and Katu (Pungent) in taste, Uṣṇa virya (Hot in potency), Rucya (Promotes taste) and Vranakṛt (Promotes complexion). It cures Diseases of Kapha doṣa, Kāsa (Cough), Chardi (Vomiting), Swāsa (Dyspnoea), Tṛṣṇā (Thrist), Kṛmi (Worm infestations) and Viṣa Posionous manifestations). Chemical composition: Volatile oils, Gums, Resins, Fats, Sugar etc. Properties and indications: Almost similar to that of Jātīphala. Mātrā (Dosage): Cūrna: 1-3gm

Explain the meaning of the following verse from Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (Karpuradi Varga, Chapter 2, verse 229):

स्रक्ष्मोपकुञ्चिका तुत्या कोरङ्गी द्राविडी त्रुटिः । एला सूक्ष्मा कफश्वासकासार्शोमूत्रकृच्छूहत् । रसे तु कटुका शीता लघ्वी वातहरी मता ।।६३।।
answer_text: Digestive diseases: Cold infusion of Bhadrailā is used to treat Ajīrna (Indigestion), Aruchi (Anorexia) and Ādmāna (Flatulance). Respiratory disease: The powder of the seed is given in appopriate dose with Madhu to treat cough. Eye diseases: The aromatic oil extracted from the seeds is applied to the Netrakopa (Conjunctivitis) External uses: The paste of the seeds of Bhrahadelā is applied externally over skin diseases like Viccharchika (Eczema), Dadru(Ringworm) etc. Flavouring agent: The Extracted oil mixed with many preparation to give pleasant odor. Mātrā (Dosage): Bīja cūrṇa 1-3gms. SŪKSMĀELĀ Latin: Elattaria cardamomum Maton. Fam: Zingiberaceae Hin: Chotielachi Eng: Lessar Cardamon Paryāyanāma (Synonyms): Sūksmā, Upakuñcikā, Tuttā, Korangū, Drāvidī and Trti. Guṇa karma (Properties and indications): It cures diseases of Kapha, Swāsa (Dyspnoea), Kāsa (Cough), Arśas (Piles) and Mūtrakṛcchra (Dysuria). It is Kaṭu (Bitter) in taste, Sīta vīrya (Cold in potency), Laghu (Light for digestion) and Subsides Vāta. Utpattisthāna (Natural territory): It is widely found.in Western Ghats of southern India and cultivated above 2500-5000 ft. Swarūpa (Botanical description): An evergreen perineal herb growing upto 2-4 m.in high with thick spreading elongated and greenish rhizomes. Leaves are 20-40cm. long, alternately arranged in two ranks, linear lanceolate, green glabrous with pointed tip. Flower are white streaked with violet arranged in pannicles 1-2 ft long.Fruits- capsule, 1-2cm long, trigonous, yellow green in colour and contains several blackish-brown seeds. Prayojya aṅga (Part used): Bīja (Seeds). Chemical constituents: Essential oil contains- Terpinene, Limonene, Menthone Terpineol, Terpimylacctate, Cineol, Starch and Proteins
citation: Bhavaprakasha Nighantu — Karpuradi Varga, Chapter 2, verse 229
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Karpuradi Varga, Chapter 2, verse 229.

answer_text: Urinary disease: The infusion prepared from fruits is effective Mūtrala (Diuretic) useful in Mūtraghāta (Retention of urine), Mūtrakṛchra (Dysuria) etc. External uses: The extracted leaf juice is applied externally over Mukhapāka (Stomatitis), Vrna (Wounds) etc. Mātrā (Dosage): Phala cūrna: 3-6 gms, Kwātha: 50-100ml. LAGUPAÑCAMÜLA Sālparṇī, Pṛsniparṇī, Bṛhatī, Kanṭakāri and Gōkṣurā all togetherly known as Laghu Pañchamūla. These are Laghu (Light for digestion), Swādu (Palatable), Bala Karaka (Strength promoters), subsides Vāṭa and Pitta doṣa, Nati usna (Not excessive hot in potency) Bṛhmaṇa (Stoutning) and Grāhī (Absorbents). it cures Jvara (Fever), Swāsa (Dysponea)and Aśmari (Renal calculi). Bṛhat and Lagu pañcamūla togetherly known as Daśamūla. It is useful in diseases of Tridoshaja origin, Swāsa (Dysponea), Kāsa (Cough), Udaraśūla (Head ache), Tandrā (Delerium), Sotha (Inflammation), Jvara (Fever), Ānāha (Flatulence), Pāśva śūla (Pain in flanks) and Aruchi (Aneroxia)

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (Puspa Varga, Chapter 4, verse 499):

नेपाली कथिता तज्झैः सप्तला नवमालिका । वासन्ती श्रीतला लघ्वी तिक्ता दोषत्रयास्त्रजित् ।।१४११
answer_text: Diseases of Eye: The extract of the rose petals is used as drops or eye wash in Netradāha (Burning sensation of the eyes). Digestive disease: The dried paste of the petals of rose is taken internally along with milk to treat Urdhvaga amla Pitta (Gastritis) and Grahanī (Spure). The decoction prepared from the rose buds is used to treat Vibanda (Constipation). Rosehip tincture is an effective astringent for treating Ātisarā (Diarrhoea), Sūla (Abdominal colic) and Kāsa (Cough). Diseases of oral cavity: A gargle made from petal infusion of rose is used for Galaroga (Sore throats). External uses: The paste of the rose petals or the powder of the dried petals is applied over the Vṛṇa (Wounds) for quicker healing. The paste of the petals is applied over the body to control Swedadikya (Excessive sweating) and to give a pleasant smell. Mātrā (Dosage): Cūrna 1-3gms., Arka: 20-40ml. VĀSANTĪ Latin: Jasminum arborescens Roxb. Fam: Oleaceae Hin: Nevari ng: Tree jasmine Paryāyanāma (Synonyms): Nepāli, Saptalā and Navamālikā. Guṇa karma (Properties and indications): Vāsantī is Śīta vīrya (Cold in potency), Laghu (Light for digestion), Tiktā (Bitter) in taste, it cures diseases of Tri doṣa and Rakta. Utpattisthāna (Natural territory): It is found in tropical Himalayas and Deccan Peninsula at an altitudes of 200-1000 m. Swarūpa (Botanical description): It is climbing shrub, with hairy branches. Leaves are simple, oppositely arranged, ovate, acuminate apex, round base, variable in size, upto 18 cm by 10 cm. across. Flowers are arranged in cymes white and fragrant. Fruit berry 1-1.5 cm long, ellipsoid, black when ripe. Chemical constituents: Volatile oils

answer_text: Fam: Sapotaceae Latin: Mimusops elengi Linn. Hin: Mulsari ng: Spanish cherry Paryāyanāma (Synonyms): Madhugandha and Simha kesaraka. Guṇa karma (Properties and indications): Bakul is Kaṣāya (Astringent) and Kaṭu (Pungent) in taste, Kaṭu vipāka (Pungent in post digestive), and Anuṣṇa (Mild hot in potency). It cures Diseases of Kapha and Pitta, Vişa (Posionous manifestations), Świtra ( (Vitiligo), Kṛmi (Worm infestations) and Danta roga (Dental diseases). Paryāyanāma (Synonyms): Śivamallī, Pāśupaṭa, Ekāṣthīlā, Vako and Vasu. Guṇa karma (Properties and indications): Baka is Anuṣṇa (Mild hot in potency), Kaṭu (Pungent), Tiktā (Bitter) in taste, it cures diseases of Kapha Pitta, Viṣa (Posionous manifestations), Yoni śūla (Uterine colic), Tṛṣṇā (Thrist), Dāha (Burning sensation), Kuṣṭa (Leprosy), Śotha (Inflammation) and Diseases of Rakta. Utpattisthāna (Natural territory): Found wild in the forests of southern India and Burma. Swarūpa (Botanical description): It is an evergreen tree growing upto 16 m.Bark is rough and dark grey. Leaves are 5–14 cm. long and 2.5–6 cm. wide, glossy, ellipticaloblong, accuminate apex, round base and wavy margins. Flowers are creamy white, hairy, scented, star shaped in axillary fasicles. Fruit -Berry, ellipsoid, reddish-brown when ripe, one seeded. Prayojya aṅga (Part used): Twak (Bark), Puṣpā (Flowers) and Phala (Fruits). Chemical constituents: The leaves of the plant Bakula contain sterols, tannins and reducing sugars, D-Mannitol, beta sitosterol and D- glycoside, pentacyclic triterpene acids and mimusopic acid

answer_text: Latin: Thespesia populnea Soland ex Correa. Fam: Malvaceae Hin: Paras pipal Eng: Umbrella tree, Indian tulip tree Paryāyanāma (Synonyms): Pārīṣa Palāśa, Kapicūta, Kamanḍalu, Gardhabhāṇḍa, Kandarāla, Kapītana and Supārśvaka. Guṇa karma (Properties and indications): Pārīṣa is Durjarā (Difficult to digest), Snigdha (Oilyness), Enances Kṛmi (Worm), Sukra (Seman), and Kapha. Its fruits are Amala (Sour) in taste, Roots are Madhurā (Sweet), Fruit pulp is Kaṣāya (Astringent) and Swādu (Plaltable). Utpattisthāna (Natural territory): Found in costal parts of India, forests and road sides. Botanical description (Swarūpa): It is medium sized evergreen tree reaches upto 15m.high. Bark fissured dark- brown in colour. Leaves simple, 8-22cm.long, alternately arranged, ovate- cordate and accuminate apex. Flowers are arranged in axillary, solitary, cymes, yellow in colour: Fruit capsule, globose or subglobose, shortly beaked, indehiscent. 43 JA-413 Prayojya aṅga (Part used): Twak (Bark), Phala (Fruit). Chemical constituents: Populinin, Populnetin, Herbecetin

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (Saka Varga, Chapter 9, verse 890):

पिण्डारं शीतलं बल्यं पित्तघं रुचिकारकम् । पार्के लघ् विशेषेण विषशान्तिकरं स्मृतम् ।।८५.)।
answer_text: Urinary disease: Fruit being a Mūtrala (Diuretic) effective in the treatment of Sotha (Inflammation) and Aśmari (Renal calculi). Acoholic poisioning: The rind of the fruit is used in cases of Madataya (Alcoholic poisoning). Purgative action: The roots are Recaka (Purgative) and in large dose is said to be a Vamaka (Emetic). Latin: Randia uliginosa DC. Fam: Rubiaceae Hin: Pindar Eng: Divine jasmine Guṇa karma (Properties and indications): Pinḍāra fruit is Sīta vīrya (Cold in potency), Balya (Promotes strength), Increases pitta dosa, Laghu (Light for digestion) and especially useful in Viṣa (Posionous manifestations). Utpattisthāna (Natural territory): It grows towards banks of rivers and other moist places in eastern, western, central and southern parts of india. Swarūpa (Botanical description): It is a tall shrub or small tree reaches about 7m. Stem four angled. Leaves 5-20 cm.long and 2-10 cm wide simple, opposite, obovate or oblong, cuneate base, apex round and entire margins. Flowers are dimorphic, large, solitary, sessile, white Fruit is a berry, 4-5 cm.long and 2.5-3.5 cm. wide, ovoid or ellipsoid, smooth, yellow contains smooth compressed seeds. Chemical constituents: Saponin, Olenolic acid, lucocyanidin, mannitol and essential oils

Guna karma (Properties and indications): Vartaka meat is Agnikar (Appetizer), Śīta vīrya (Cold in potency), cures Jwara (Fever), subsides all dosas, Rucya (Promotes taste), Sukrada (Increases seman), Balya (Promotes strength). Vartakā meat has possess lesser qualties. Lava (Common quail)

explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Mamsa Varga, Chapter 10, verse 930.

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (Takra Varga, Chapter 15, verse 1021):

घोल तु मथित तक्रमुदश्चिच्छाच्छिकाऽपि च । ससर निर्जल घोल मथित त्वसरोदकम् ।।१।। तक्रं पादजलं प्रोक्तमुदश्चित्वर्द्धवारिकमु । छच्छिका सारहीना स्यात्स्वच्छा प्रचुरवारिका । घोलं तु शर्करायुक्त गुणैल्लेयं रसालवत् ।।२११ घोलं तु शर्करायुक्त गुणैज़यं रसालवत् । वातपित्तहरं ह्रादि मथितं कफपित्तनुत् ।।३।। तक्र ग्राहि कषायाम्ल स्वादु पाकरस लघु । वीर्योष्ण दीपन वृष्य प्रीणन वातनाशनम् ।।४।। ग्रहण्यादिमता पथ्यं भवेत्सड्याहि लाघवात् । किञ्च स्वादुविपाकित्वान्न च पित्तप्रकोपणम् ।।।५।। अम्लोष्ण दीपन वृष्य प्रीणन वातनाशनम् । कषायोष्णविकाशित्वाद्रौक्ष्याच्चापि कफापहम् ।।।६।। न तक्रसेवी व्यथते कदाचिन्न तक्रदग्याः प्रभवन्ति रोगाः । यथा सुराणाममृत सुखाय तथा नराणा भुवि तक्रमाहुः ।।७।। उदश्चित् कफकृद् बल्यमामध्यं परमं मतमू । छच्छिका श्रीतला लघ्वी पित्तश्रमतृषाहरी । वातनुत् कफकृत् सा तु दीपनी लवणान्विता ।।८।। समुद्धृतघृतं तक्रं पथ्यं लघु विशेषतः ।।’९।। स्तोकोद्धतघृत तस्माद् गुरु वृष्य कफापहम् । अनुद्धतघृत सान्द्र गुरु पुष्टिकफप्रदम् ।।१०।। वातेऽम्लं शस्यते तक्रं शुण्ङ्गीसैन्यवसंयुतम् । पित्ते स्वादु सितायुक्तं व्योषक्षारयुतं कफे ।।११।। हिङ्गजीरयुतं घोलं सैन्यवेन च संयुतम् । भवेदतीव वातघ्नमर्शोऽतीसारहृत्परम् ।।१२।। रुचिद पुष्टिद बल्य वस्तिशूलविनाशनम् । मूत्रकृच्छे तु सगुडं पाण्डुरोगे सचित्रकम् ।।१३।।
answer_text: Based on their properties and differ in water proportion different names has been given - Ghola, Mathita, Takra, Udachita and Chachikā. Different names are given according to different properties and preparation methods of Takra- they are Ghola, Mathita, Takra, Udaśvit and Chacchikā. S.no Different types Method of preparation of Takras. Ghola Prepared by churning curd without removing fat and adding water. Mathita Prepared by churning curd by removing supernated fat and without adding water. Takra Prepared by churning curd by adding four parts of water. Udaśvit Prepared by churning curd by adding half part of water. Chacchikā Prepared by churning curd removing supernated fat and repeat n the content of churning by adding sufficient quantity of water. If sarkara is added into the Ghola, its properties are equavalent to Rasala. It subsides Vāta, Pitta doṣa and Aālladhajanaka (Pleasent to body and mind). Mathita subsides Kapha and Pitta doṣa. Takra is Kaṣāya (Astringent), Amla (Sour) and Madhura (Sweet) in taste, Madhura vīpaka (Sweet in post digestive), Grahī (Absorbent), Laghu (Light for digestion), Uşna vīrya (Hot in potency), Dīpana (Appetizer), Vṛṣya (Aphrodisiac), Prinanam (Satisfying) and subsides Vāta. In Grahani (Spure) etc., diseases Takra is a ideal drink, being Laghu (Light for digestion) it acts as Grahī (Absorbent), Madhura vīpaka (Pungent in post digestion) and doesn’t aggravates Pitta. Being amla rasa (Sour), Uşna vīrya (Hot in potency), Dīpana (Appetizer), Vrṣya (Aphrodisiac) and Pinana (Satisfying), it aggravates Vāta. Being as Kaşāya (Astringent), Uşna vīrya (Hot in potency), Vīkasi (immuno suppressant) and Rūṣka (Drying), it subsides Kapha. Person who consumes the Takra regularly as diet never becomes ill, diseases cured by takra do not recurved, just as amrta (divine nector) is for the gods, takra is to humans. Udaśvit increases Kapha, Balya (Promotes strength), relieves excessive Ama (Undigested food). Chacchikā is Śīta vīrya (Cold in potency), Laghu (Light for digestion), Subsides Vāta, increases Kapha. It cures Srama (Fatigue) and Tṛṣṇā (Thrist). If it is taken along with Sindhava lavana, acts as Dīpana (Appetizer). Takra which is deviod of Ghṛta is acts as Pathya (Ideal diet) and Laghu (Light for digestion). if Ghṛta is partly removed is Guru (Heavy for digestion), Vṛṣya (Aphrodisiac) and subsides Kapha and Vāta. If Ghṛta is not removed is Guru (Heavy for digestion), Pustikara (Nutrient) and Increases Kapha dosa. Usage of Takra as per Dosa andVyadhi: In case of aggravated Vāta, Amla (Sour) butter milk along with Suṇṭhī and Saiṇḍhava lavaṇa is ideal. In case of aggravated Pitta, Madhura (Sweet) butter milk along with sugar is ideal. In case of Increased Kapha, Takra along with Sunṭhi, Marica, Pippali and Yava kṣara is best. If Ghola is taken along with Hingu, Jīraka, and Saindhava lavaņa, it will increases Vāta, cures Arśas (Haemorrhoids), Atisāra (Diarrhoea), Rucya (Promotes taste), Puṣṭikara (Nutrient), Balya (Promotes strength) and Basti śūla nāṣaka (Cures bladder colic). Ghola along with guda is beneficial in Mūtrakṛcchra (Dysuria) and along with Chitraka it is good in Pāṇḍu (Anemia)
citation: Bhavaprakasha Nighantu — Takra Varga, Chapter 15, verse 1021
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Takra Varga, Chapter 15, verse 1021.

एरण्डतैल तीक्ष्णोष्णं दीपनं पिच्छिलं गुरु । वृष्यं त्वच्यं वयःस्थापि मेधाकान्तिबलप्रदम् ।।२२।। कषायानुरसं सूक्ष्मं योनिशुक्रविशोधनम् । विस्रं स्वादु रसे पाके सतिक्त कट्टकं रसम् ।।२३।। विषमज्वरह्र्र्ोगपृष्ठगुह्याादिशूलनुत् वातशोणितविड्बन्धब्रध्नशोथामविद्रधीन् । आमवातगजेन्द्रस्य शरीरवनचारिणः । एक एव निहन्ताऽयमेरण्डस्नेहकेसरी ।।२५ ।।

It cures Vişama jvara (Malaria), Hrdroga (Cardiac diseases), Pruştagudaśūla (Pain in back and anal region), Disease of Vāta, Udararoga (Abdominal diseases), Gūlma (Abdominal tumors), Aṣṭilā (Diseases of Prostate), Katigraha (Stiffness in waist regions), Vātarakta (Gout), Malabadha (Constipation), Brandha (Hernia), Sotha (Inflammation), Āma (Undigested food) and Vīdradi (Abcess). The fatal disease Āmavāta (Rheumatism) is roaming throughout the body as like an elephant in the forest, which can be controlled by the action of Eranda taila, like a loin, the majesty of wild animals. question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (Ikshu Varga, Chapter 22, verse 1066):

इक्षो रसो यः सम्पक्को जायते लोष्टवद् दृढः । स गुडो, गौडदेशे तु मत्स्यण्ड्येव गुडो मतः ।।१४।। गुडो वृष्यो गुरुः स्निग्धो वातघ्नो मूत्रशोधनः । नातिपित्तहरो मेदःकफक्रिमिबलप्रदः ।। २५.।। गुडो जीर्णो लघुः पथ्योऽनभिष्यन्द्यग्निपुष्टिकृत् । पित्तघ्नो मधुरो वृष्यो वातघ्नोऽसुक्प्रसादनः ।। २६ ।। गुडो नवः कफश्वासक्रिमिकरोऽग्निकृत् । ! २७.।। श्लेष्माणमाशु विनिहन्ति सदार्ककेण पित्तं निहन्ति च तदेव हरीतकीभिः । शुण्ङ्ग्या समं हरति वातमशेषमित्यं दोषत्रयक्षयकराय नमो गुडाय ।। २८ ।।
answer_text: Sugarcane juice boiled till it becomes hard like a stone is called as Guḍa (Jaggery). In the gouda dēśa matśyandī is know as Guḍa. Guda is Vrṣya (Aphrodisiac), Guru (Heavy for digestion), Increases vāta dosa, Mūtraśhodaka (Clears the urine), Slightly increases Pitta dosa. It aggravates Medha (Fat), Kapha dosa, leads to Krmi (Worms infestations) and gives Bāla (Strength). Purana guḍa: Purana guḍa is Laghu (Light for digestion), Pathyā (Ideal diet), Abhiṣyanḍi (Blocks the channels), Agnikrt (Appetizer), Pustivardaka (Nutrient), Subsides pitta, Madhura (Sweet) in taste, Vrṣya (Aphrodisiac), Subsides vāta doṣa and Rakta prasādhana (Purifies the blood). Naveena guda: Naveena guda aggravates Kapha, leads to diseases like Swāsa (Dyspnoea) Kāsa (Cough), Kṛmi (Worm infestations) and acts as Agnikṛt (Appetizer). Properties of guda based on anupana: If Guḍa is consumed along with Adraka, it immediately destroyes kapha dosa, along with Harītakī it subsides pitta, with śuṇṭhī cures all vātagata rogas. So salutations to Guḍa which migrates all Tridosas

question:
Fill in the blank in this verse from Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (Takra Varga, Chapter 15, verse 1021):

घोल तु मथित तक्रमुदश्चिच्छाच्छिकाऽपि च । ससर निर्जल घोल मथित त्वसरोदकम् ।।१।। तक्रं पादजलं प्रोक्तमुदश्चित्वर्द्धवारिकमु । छच्छिका सारहीना स्यात्स्वच्छा प्रचुरवारिका । घोलं तु शर्करायुक्त गुणैल्लेयं रसालवत् ।।२११ घोलं तु शर्करायुक्त गुणैज़यं रसालवत् । वातपित्तहरं ह्रादि मथितं कफपित्तनुत् ।।३।। तक्र ग्राहि कषायाम्ल स्वादु पाकरस लघु । वीर्योष्ण दीपन वृष्य प्रीणन वातनाशनम् ।।४।। ग्रहण्यादिमता पथ्यं भवेत्सड्याहि लाघवात् । किञ्च स्वादुविपाकित्वान्न च पित्तप्रकोपणम् ।।।५।। अम्लोष्ण दीपन वृष्य प्रीणन वातनाशनम् । कषायोष्णविकाशित्वाद्रौक्ष्याच्चापि कफापहम् ।।।६।। न तक्रसेवी व्यथते कदाचिन्न तक्रदग्याः प्रभवन्ति रोगाः । यथा सुराणाममृत सुखाय तथा नराणा भुवि तक्रमाहुः ।।७।। उदश्चित् कफकृद् बल्यमामध्यं परमं मतमू । छच्छिका श्रीतला लघ्वी पित्तश्रमतृषाहरी । वातनुत् ________ सा तु दीपनी लवणान्विता ।।८।। समुद्धृतघृतं तक्रं पथ्यं लघु विशेषतः ।।’९।। स्तोकोद्धतघृत तस्माद् गुरु वृष्य कफापहम् । अनुद्धतघृत सान्द्र गुरु पुष्टिकफप्रदम् ।।१०।। वातेऽम्लं शस्यते तक्रं शुण्ङ्गीसैन्यवसंयुतम् । पित्ते स्वादु सितायुक्तं व्योषक्षारयुतं कफे ।।११।। हिङ्गजीरयुतं घोलं सैन्यवेन च संयुतम् । भवेदतीव वातघ्नमर्शोऽतीसारहृत्परम् ।।१२।। रुचिद पुष्टिद बल्य वस्तिशूलविनाशनम् । मूत्रकृच्छे तु सगुडं पाण्डुरोगे सचित्रकम् ।।१३।।

question:
Read the following verse from Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (Takra Varga, Chapter 15, verse 1021):

घोल तु मथित तक्रमुदश्चिच्छाच्छिकाऽपि च । ससर निर्जल घोल मथित त्वसरोदकम् ।।१।। तक्रं पादजलं प्रोक्तमुदश्चित्वर्द्धवारिकमु । छच्छिका सारहीना स्यात्स्वच्छा प्रचुरवारिका । घोलं तु शर्करायुक्त गुणैल्लेयं रसालवत् ।।२११ घोलं तु शर्करायुक्त गुणैज़यं रसालवत् । वातपित्तहरं ह्रादि मथितं कफपित्तनुत् ।।३।। तक्र ग्राहि कषायाम्ल स्वादु पाकरस लघु । वीर्योष्ण दीपन वृष्य प्रीणन वातनाशनम् ।।४।। ग्रहण्यादिमता पथ्यं भवेत्सड्याहि लाघवात् । किञ्च स्वादुविपाकित्वान्न च पित्तप्रकोपणम् ।।।५।। अम्लोष्ण दीपन वृष्य प्रीणन वातनाशनम् । कषायोष्णविकाशित्वाद्रौक्ष्याच्चापि कफापहम् ।।।६।। न तक्रसेवी व्यथते कदाचिन्न तक्रदग्याः प्रभवन्ति रोगाः । यथा सुराणाममृत सुखाय तथा नराणा भुवि तक्रमाहुः ।।७।। उदश्चित् कफकृद् बल्यमामध्यं परमं मतमू । छच्छिका श्रीतला लघ्वी पित्तश्रमतृषाहरी । वातनुत् कफकृत् सा तु दीपनी लवणान्विता ।।८।। समुद्धृतघृतं तक्रं पथ्यं लघु विशेषतः ।।’९।। स्तोकोद्धतघृत तस्माद् गुरु वृष्य कफापहम् । अनुद्धतघृत सान्द्र गुरु पुष्टिकफप्रदम् ।।१०।। वातेऽम्लं शस्यते तक्रं शुण्ङ्गीसैन्यवसंयुतम् । पित्ते स्वादु सितायुक्तं व्योषक्षारयुतं कफे ।।११।। हिङ्गजीरयुतं घोलं सैन्यवेन च संयुतम् । भवेदतीव वातघ्नमर्शोऽतीसारहृत्परम् ।।१२।। रुचिद पुष्टिद बल्य वस्तिशूलविनाशनम् । मूत्रकृच्छे तु सगुडं पाण्डुरोगे सचित्रकम् ।।१३।।

पञ्चानां पञ्चमूळानां भागान् दशपलोन्मितान् । हरीतकीसहस्रं च त्रिगुणामलकं नवम् ॥ ४१ ॥ शालपर्णीं बृहतीं पृश्निपर्णीं निदिग्धिकाम् । विद्याद्विदारिगन्धाद्यं श्वदंष्ट्रापञ्चमं गणम् ॥ ४२ ॥ बिल्वाग्निमन्थश्योनाकं काश्मर्यमथ पाटलाम् । पुनर्नवां मुद्गपर्णीं माषपर्णीं बलामेरण्डमेव च ॥ ४३ ॥ जीवकर्षभकौ मेदां जीवन्तीं सशतावरीम् । शरेक्षुदर्भकाशानां शालीनां मूलमेव च ॥ ४४ ॥ इत्येषां पञ्चमूळानां पञ्चानामुपकल्पयेत् । भागान् यथोक्तांस्तत्सर्वं साध्यं दशगुणेऽम्भसि ॥ ४५ ॥ दशभागावशिष्टं तु पूतं तं ग्राहयेद्रसम् । हरीतकीश्च ताः सर्वाः सर्वाण्यामलकानि च ॥ ४६ ॥ तानि सर्वाण्यनस्थीनि फलान्यापोथ्य कूर्चैः । क्षिप्त्वा तस्मिन्निर्यूहे चूर्णानीमानि दापयेत् ॥ ४७ ॥ मण्डूकपर्ण्योः पिप्पल्याः शङ्खपुष्प्याः प्लवस्य च । मुस्तानां सविडङ्गानां चन्दनागुरुयोस्तथा ॥ ४८ ॥ मधुकस्य हरिद्रायाः वचाया नागकेसरस्य च । भागांश्चतुष्पलान् कृत्वा सूक्ष्मैलायास्त्वचस्तथा ॥ ४९ ॥ सितोपलासहस्रं च चूर्णितं तैलस्याढकं । दद्यात्त्रीणि च सर्पिषः ॥ ५० ॥ साध्यमौदुम्बरे पात्रे तत्सर्वं मृद्वग्निना । क्वाथं लेहवदग्निं च शीतं क्षौद्रेण संयोजयेत् ॥ ५१ ॥ क्षौद्रार्धं तत्सर्वं घृतभाजने । तिष्ठेत्संरक्षितं तस्य मात्रां काले प्रयोजयेत् ॥ ५२ ॥ या नोपरुन्ध्यादाहारमेवं मात्रां जयां प्रति । षष्टिकः पयसा चात्र जीर्णे भोज्यमिष्यते ॥ ५३ ॥ वैखानसा बालखिल्यास्तथा चान्ये तपोधनाः । रसायनमिदं प्राप्य बहुक्षरमितायुषः ॥ ५ ४ ॥ मुक्त्वा जीर्णं वपुः प्रथमवपुस्तरुणे वयः । वीततन्द्राश्रमश्वासा निरातङ्काः समाहिताः ॥ ५५ ॥ मेधास्मृतिबलैर्युक्ताश्चिरं राष्ट्र तपोधनाः । ब्राह्मं तपोऽथ ब्रह्मचर्यं स्वेच्छात्यन्तनिष्ठया ॥ ५६ ॥ रसायनमिदं ब्राह्ममायुष्कामो प्रयोजयेत् । दीर्घमायुष्यमश्राम्यं कामं श्रेष्ठं समश्नुते ॥ ५७ ॥

context: प्रयोजयेज्ज्वरहरान्निरूहान् सानुवासनान् । पक्वाशयगते दोषे वक्ष्यन्ते ये च सिद्धिस्य ॥ २४० ॥ पटोलारिष्टपत्राणि, सोशीरं ह्यश्वतुरङ्गकम् । हीवेरं, रोहिणी, तिक्ता, श्वदंष्ट्रा, मदनानि, च ॥ २४१ ॥ स्थिरा बला च तत् सर्वं पयस्यर्धादके शृतम् । क्षीरावशेषं निर्यूहे संयुक्तं मधुसर्पिषा ॥ २४२ ॥ कल्कमदनमुस्तानां पिप्पल्या मधुकस्य च । वत्सकस्य च संयुक्तं बस्तिं दद्याज्ज्वरापहम् ॥ २४३ ॥ शुद्धे मार्गे हते दोषे विप्रसन्नेषु धातुषु । गताङ्गशूले लघ्वङ्गः सद्यो भवति विज्वरः ॥ २४४ ॥ आरग्वधमुशीरं च मदनस्य फलं तथा । चतस्रः पर्णिनीश्चैव निर्यूहेमुपकल्पयेत् ॥ २४५ ॥ प्रियङ्गुमदनमुस्तशताह्वामधुयष्टिका । कल्कः सर्पिर्गुडः क्षौद्रं ज्वरघ्नो बस्तिरुत्तमः ॥ २४६ ॥ गुडूचीं त्रायमाणां च चन्दनं मधुकं वचाम् । स्थिरां बलां पृश्निपर्णी मदनं चेति साधयेत् ॥ २४७ ॥ रसं जाङ्गळमांसस्य तेन, सहितं भिषक् । पिप्पळीफलमुस्तानां, कल्केन, मधुकस्य, च ॥ २४८ ॥ ईषत्सलवणं च युक्त्या तेनिरूहं च मधुसर्पिषा । ज्वरप्रशमनं कुर्याद्वलस्वेदरुचिमदम् ॥ २४९ ॥ जीवन्ती मधुकं मेदां पिप्पळीं मदनं वचाम् । ऋद्धिं रास्नां बलां विश्वं शतपुष्पां शतावरीम् ॥ २५० ॥ पिष्ट्वा क्षीरं जलं सर्पिस्तैलं च विपचेद्भिषक् । आनुवासनिकं स्नेहमेतं विद्याज्ज्वरापहम् ॥ २५१ ॥ तथा पटोलनिम्बामृद्वीभ्यां, गुडूच्या, मधुकेन च । मदनैश्च शृतः स्नेहो ज्वरघ्नोऽनुवासनम् ॥ २५२ ॥ चन्दनागुरुकाश्मर्यपटोलमधुकोत्पलैः । सिद्धः स्नेहो ज्वरहरः स्नेहबस्तिः प्रशस्यते ॥ २५३ ॥

वातजे श्रमजे चैव पुराणे क्षतजे ज्वरे । लङ्घनं न हितं विद्याच्छमनैस्तानुपाचरेत् ॥ २७२ ॥ विक्षिप्यामाशयोष्माणं यस्माद्रत्वा रसं नृणाम् । ज्वरं कुर्वन्ति दोषास्तु हीयतेऽग्निबलं ततः ॥ २७३ ॥ यथा प्रज्वलितो वह्निः स्थाल्यामिन्धनवानपि । न पचत्योदनं सम्यग्विनिष्प्रेरितो बहिः ॥ २७४ ॥ पक्तिस्थानात्तथा दोषैर्विक्षिप्तो वह्निरेवणाम् । न पचत्यन्नवहतं कृच्छ्रात् पचति वा लघु ॥ २७५ ॥ अतोऽग्निबलरक्षार्थं लङ्घनादिक्रमो हितः । सप्ताहेन हि पच्यन्ते सप्तधातुगता मलाः ॥ २७६ ॥ निरामत्वाप्यतः प्रोक्तो ज्वरः प्रायोऽष्टमेऽहनि । उदीर्णाग्निस्त्वप्यन्निरश्नन् गुरु विशेषतः ॥ २७७ ॥ मुच्यते सहसा प्राणैश्चिरं क्लिश्यति वा नरः । तस्मात्कारणाद्विद्वान् वातिकेऽप्यादितो ज्वरे ॥ २७८ ॥ नाति गुर्वति वा स्निग्धं भोजयेत् सहसा नरम् । ज्वरे मारुतजे त्वादावनपेक्ष्यापि हि क्रमम् ॥ २७९ ॥ कुर्यान्निर्बन्धनानामभ्यङ्गादीनुपक्रमान् । पाययित्वा च कषायं न चान्नं भोजयेद्रसभोजनम् ॥ २८० ॥ जीर्णज्वरहरं कुर्यात् सर्वं चाप्युपक्रमम् । श्लेष्मलानामवातानां ज्वरोऽनुष्णः कफाधिकः ॥ २८१ ॥ परिपाकं न सप्तादिनापि याति मृदूष्मणाम् । तं क्रमेण यथोक्तेन लङ्घनाल्पाशनादिना ॥ २८२ ॥ आदशाहमुपक्रम्य कषायैश्चोपचरेत् ।

context: क्रियातिवृत्ते जठरे, त्रिदोषे, चाप्रशाम्यति ॥ १७५ ॥ ब्रातीन् ससुह्वदो दार'न् ब्राह्मणान् नृपतीन् गुरून् । अनुब्राप्य, भिषक् (कर्म), विदृध्यात् (संशयं, ब्रुवन् ॥ १७६ ॥ अक्रियायां ध्रुवो मृत्युः क्रियायां संशयो भवेत् । पवमाख्याय तस्येदमनुक्षातः सुद्दद्रणैः ॥ १७७ । पानभोजनसंयुक्त विषमस्मै प्रयोजयेत् । यस्मिन् वा कुपितः सर्पो विखजेद्वि फर्ने विषम् ॥ १७८ । भोजयेत्तहुद्रिणं प्रविचार्य भिषग्वरः । तेनास्य दोषसङ्कातः स्थिरो लीनो विमार्गगः ॥ १७९ ॥ विषेणासुप्रमाथित्वादाशु – भिन्नः – प्रवर्तते । विषेणा हृतदोष – तं शीताम्बुपरिषेचितम ॥ १८० ॥ पाययेत भिषग्दुग्धं यवागूं वा यथाबल्रम् । त्रिवृत्मण्डूकपर्ण्योश्व शाकं सयववास्तुकम् ॥ १८१ ॥ भक्षयेत् कालशार्क वा स्वरसोदकसाधितम् । निरम्छलवणस्नैद स्विन्नास्विन्नमननभुक ॥ १८२ ॥ मासमेक ततश्चैव तृषितः स्वरसं पिवेत् । पवं, विनिहंते, दोषे, शाकैर्मासात्, परं, ततः ॥ १८३ ॥ दुर्बल्लाय प्रयुश्रीत प्राणभ्वत् कारभं पयः । इदं तु शब्यहतंणां कर्म स्याद्वष्टकर्मणाम् ॥ १८४ ॥ वामं कुश्नि मापयित्वा नाम्यधतुरङ्कलम् । मात्रायुक्तेन श्रुषण पाटयेन्मतिमान् भिषक ॥ १८५ ॥ विपाट्यान्त्र ततः पथ्याद्वीक्ष्य बद्धक्षतान्त्रयोः । सपिंषाऽस्यज्य केशादीनवमृज्य विमोक्षयेत् ॥ १८६ ॥ मूछेनायच संमूढमन्त्र तच विमोक्षयेत् । छिद्राण्यन्त्रस्य तु स्थूलैर्देशयित्वा पिपीलिकैं ॥ १८७ ॥ दहुशाः संग्रहीतानि ब्रात्वा च्छित्वा पिपीलिकान् । प्रतियोगैः प्रवेष्यान्त्र प्रेयैः सीव्येद्वरणं ततः ॥१८८॥

context: श्रावणीक्षीरकाकोलीजीवकर्षभकेः समैः । सिद्धं समधुकेः सर्पिः सक्षीरं, वातरकन्वत् ॥ ५५ ॥ बल्टामतिवलों मेदामात्मगुप्तां शतावरीम् । काकोलों क्षीरकाकोलों रास्तामृद्धि च पेषयेत् ॥ ५६ ॥ चतुर्गुणक्षीरं - तैः सिद्धं वातरक्तजुत् । हृत्पाण्डुरोगवीसर्पकामलाज्वरनाशनम् ॥ ५७ ॥ घट्टते ह त्रायन्तिका तामलक्री द्विकाकोली शतावरी । कशेरुकाकषायेण, कल्कैरेभिः पचेद्घृतम् ॥ ५८ ॥ दस्वी परूषकद्राक्षाकाइमयेंधुरसान् समान् । पृथग्विदार्याः स्वरसं तथा क्षीरंतचतुर्गुणमू ॥ ५९ ॥ पतत् प्रायोगिक सर्पिः पारूषकमिति स्मृतम् । वातरक्ते क्षते रक्षीणे वीसर्पे पैस्तिके ज्वरे ॥ ६० ॥ त इति पारुषकं घृतम् । वे II पश्चमूले वर्षाभूमेरण्डं सपुनर्नवम् । मुद्गपणी महामेदां मापपणी शतावरीम् ॥ ६१ ॥ राह्नपुष्पीमचाक्पुष्पीं राज्ञामतिवळां बलाम् । पृथग्धिपलिकं कत्वा जलद्रोणे विपाचयेत् ॥ ६२ ॥ पादशेपे समान् क्षीरधात्रीक्षुच्छागलान् रसान् । घृताढकेन संयोज्य शनैम्रृद्वम्निना पचेत् ॥ ६३ ॥ कल्कानावाण्य मेदे व्रे काइमर्यफलमुत्पलम् । त्वकक्षीरीं पिप्पलीं द्राक्षां प्रमबीजं पुनर्नवाम् ॥ ६४ ॥ नागरं क्षीरकाकोल्लो पद्मक वृहतीद्वयम् । वीरां श्ट्ड्लाटकं भव्यमुरुमाणं निकोचकम् ॥ ६५ ॥ खर्जू राक्षोटवाताम नुआताभिषु कांस्तथा । पतैर्घृताढके । सिद्धेर क्षौद्रं , शीते, प्रदापयेत् ॥ ६६ ॥ सम्यक सिद्धं च विज्ञाय सुग्रतं संनिधापयेत् । कतरक्षाविधि चौक्षे प्राशयेदक्षसंमितम् ॥ ६७ ॥ पाण्डरोगं ज्वरं हिकां स्वरभेद भगन्दरम् । पार्थवेशूल्ट क्षयं कासं प्लीहानं वातशोणितम् ॥ ६८ ॥ क्षतशोषमपस्मारमइमरीं , शर्करां , तथा । सर्वाङ्गेकाङ्गरोगांध के मूत्रसङ्गंध चर नाशयेत् ॥ ६९ ॥ बलवर्णकरंगी धन्यंत्र वलीपलितनाशनम् । जीवनीयमिर्देश सर्पिर्वष्यंत्र वन्ध्यासुतप्रदम् ॥ ७० ॥ हति जीवनीयघूतम् ।

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidanam (Part 1) (Purvārdḍha, Chapter 8, verse 7):

हलिमकस्य लक्षणं विस्तरेणोक्तम् ।।७।।
answer_text: The signs and symptoms of Halimaka, an advanced stage of Pāṇḍu (anaemia), are described. This condition involves severe depletion of tissues and may present with additional complications beyond those seen in earlier stages. Signs and symptoms of Sannipāta type of Pāṇḍu The patient of of Pandu caused due to Sannipata (aggravation of all three Dosas equally), has fever, anorexia, nausea, vomitting, thirst and fatigue. He is emaciated and his organs do not perform the functions and such a patient should be discarded. Pāṇdvadiroganidānaṃ Mecaka is a black precious stone made into fine powder or paste. Anjana is Sauvīrāñjana (stybnites-collyrium). When all types of Raktapitta are caused by vi¬ tiated Pitta, how come there is separate enumeration of Pitta type of Raktapitta? It is true, but the disease originating Pitta, when gets associated with the Pitta of other places or when there is no association of other two Dosas in manifestation of Raktapitta, then it is labelled as Raktapitta of Pitta type. Pure Pitta type of Raktapitta does not at all occur; as it will be told further in this chapter that upward Raktapitta is associated with Kapha and the downward one, with Vata. It is also not be taken for granted regarding the route and Dosa-afflication. It is said that when Kapha or Vata are vitiated due to reasons pertaining to their individual vitiation, there will be association of these Dosas with the related symptomatology and not the route re¬ lated Dosa association, Upward Raktapitta is associated with Kapha only because that route belongs to Kapha and same is the case with Vata association in down¬ ward Raktapitta. In these conditions Kapha and Vata will not have individuality, like in the case of fever occuring in Sarat (moonlight season) is caused by Pitta which vitiates during that particular season and it also shows the symptoms of Kapha just because Kapha is prevalant in Sarat. As said in ''Pitta does (cause disease) in Sarat with association of Kapha.'' (Ca. ci. 3). Therefore which ever (disease) is presented with one Dosa symptoms it is caused by single dosa. In the same way the dual and Dosa triad are to be understood. Hence the upward and downward Raktapitta can be presented with single Dosa, Dosa-duo or Dosa-triad. By this the argument that the manifestation of Raktapitta in the Pitta direction is not shown, is nullified. Special Note- The material that comes out in the form of bleeding itself is called Raktapitta. Which is not liked by crows and dogs. Doşa–relation in Raktapitta
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Purvārdḍha, Chapter 8, verse 7.

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidanam (Part 1) (Nidanasthana, Chapter 4, verse 19):

विद्यादत्रातिसारवत् ।।१८ 11 निरामं दोषं साम लिड़ैरसाध्यो ग्रहणीविकारो यैस्तैरतीसारगदो न सिध्येत् । वृद्धस्य नून यहणीविकारो हत्वा तनुं नैव निवर्तते च ।।१९।।
answer_text: Saṅgraha Grahaṇī is caused by Amavāta and has the following symptomatology sounds in the intestines, lassitude, weakness, weak digestive fire and defaecation in liquid form-cold in touch solid, some times-oily with pain in low back region- unformed stool abundant-sticky-with sounds and mild pain. This disease repeats once in 15 days, 30 days, 10 days or once in a day. This aggravates during day time and pacifies in nights. It is very difficult to diagnose this disease and also difficult for cure. This afflicts the individuals for a long time. The Grahaṇīroga in which the patient sleeps always, feels pain in the flanks and makes the sound of water pouring out of a pot while defaecating, is called Ghatiyantra Grahaṇī which is incurable. Prognosis of Grahanīroga The Sāma (undigested) and Nirāma (digested) (–unformed and formed in other words) stages of the Dosas which is mentioned in Atīsāra is applicable in Grahaniroga also. Same is the case regarding incurability
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidanasthana, Chapter 4, verse 19.

answer_text: Chardi is of five types, viz., caused by Vata, Pitta, Kapha, Sannipata and by looking at hatred things etc., The symptomatology of these five types will be ex¬ plained. It is caused by consuming more liquids, more oily foods, unpleasant foods, salty foods; due to eating untimely in higher doses and in incompatible foods; due to over exertion, fear, anxiety due to indigestion, worm-infestation, in pregnant women, due to eating very speedily and also due to things that cause hatred. The Doşas suddenly come to the mouth, fill it and are expelled forcibly giving pain to all parts of the body. This process is called Chardi (vomiting). 1, 2, 3, 4 (Su. u. 49) Chardi is being explained after Arocaka as Arocaka is seen in Chardi and as also Arocaka is of five types. Bībhatsālocana is seeing uncommon things. By using the word adi (etc., ) it is implied that foul smells and eating foods which are not liked by the individual also cause Chardi. Chardi in pregnant women is caused by the pressure of the foetus on the stomach. Prodromata of Chardi Nausea, hinderance of belching, dribbling of thin and salty saliva, disliking foods and drinks are the prodromata of Chardi

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidanam (Part 1) (Nidanasthana, Chapter 22, verse 58):

वातशोणितजः शोथो जानुमध्ये महारुजः ।।५८।।
answer_text: Viśvācī ca’’–by using the word ‘‘Ca’’ (also) here, it is implied that Gṛdhrasī and Viśvācī are also called Khalli according to Gayadāsa, as there is a common symptom in these diseases i.e., shaking the affected part. This is supported by the statement of Hārīta, ''Khallī'' is also called Viśvācī and Gṛdhrasī which is associated with severe pain. 3 ' Cakrapāni said–Khallī in Caraka, is characterised by the shaking of legs calves, thighs and shoulders (Cā. cī. 28). Thus Khallī is mentioned differently from Visvācī. Susruta did not mention Khallī at all. He did not mention many diseases which are given in other treatises including the diseases caused by the covering of Vāta varieties among themselves which are mentioned in Caraka. Due to the severe pain being common feature in Visvaci and Grdhasi they are given the synonym, Khalli. It is also seen that some diseases look like other diseases as-Asthila to Pratyaṣṭhīla, Aśmarī to Śarkarā and Pāṇḍu to Kāmalā. Krostukasīrṣa (inflammed knee) The inflammation caused by Vāta and Śoṇṭā (blood) in the knee joint which is very painful is known as Krostukasirsa. The knee joint becomes big (swollen) and looks like the head of a jackal. 58 (Su. ni. 1)
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidanasthana, Chapter 22, verse 58.
context: वातशोणितजः शोथो जानुमध्ये महारुजः ।।५८।।

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidanam (Part 2) (Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 33, verse 26):

मधुकोशः उपेक्षया हि पित्तकफाजानामपि मधुमेहत्वं प्रर्वशयितुमाह-सर्व एवेत्यादि। धातुक्षयावरणाभ्यां कुपितवातेन मधुमेहसंभवमाह-मधुमेह 'इत्यादि। मधुसममिति। 'मूत्रम्' इति शेषः । स इति मधुमेहः सावरणालिङ्गमाह-आवृत इत्यादि। आवृत इति। आवृतवातकृतः। दोषलिङ्ग़नीति। येन पित्तादिना आवृतस्तस्य वातस्य च लिङ्ग़नि प्रदर्शयति। अनिमित्तमकस्मात्। क्षणात् क्षणात्पूर्ण इति। आवरणेन पुनः पूर्णो भवन् कृच्छ्साध्यो भवति। तथा च-चरकः-‘स मारुतस्य पित्तस्य कफस्य च मुहुर्मुहुः। दर्शयत्याकृतिं गत्वा क्षयमाप्याय्यते पुनः॥’ (च. सू. अ. १७) इति। धातुक्षयकुपितवातजस्य तु केवलवातजमेव लिङ्कम्। गदाधरस्त्वाह-'मधुमेहः सावरणवायुनैव क्रियते।’ यदाह-चरकः-‘तैरावृतगतिर्वायुरोज आदाय गच्छति। यदा बस्ति तदा कृच्छो मधुमेहः प्रवर्तते।’ (च. सू. अ. १७) इति। केवलवातजेष् तु कषायादिवमनाद्यतियोगादिकृतेष् धातुक्षयजेष् वायोरावरणं नास्तीति भेदः। मधुमेह शब्दप्रवृत्तिमाह-मधुरं यच्च मेहेष्वित्यादि॥ २३-२६॥ मधुरं यच्च मेहेषु प्रायो मध्विव मेहति। सर्वेऽपि मधुमेहाख्या माधुर्याच्च तनोरतः॥ २६॥ ( वा. नि. १० )
answer_text: To make it clear that leaving without treating the pitta and kapha pramehas make them also madhumeha - this stanza, “sarva eva pramehāstu….” is mentioned here. Madhumeha occurs due to aggravated vata either by emaciation of tissues or by obstruction or covering caused by other dosa or dhatus. The adjective madhu samaṃ (eqreal to or like honey) is applicable to the urine. It manifests the Vāta symptoms and also those of the covering dosa - pitta or kapha; without any reason - means suddenly. At one moment the manifestation of vāṭa is weakness and at another moment is full which makes the situation incurable. In Caraka also, it is mentioned, “The pitta and kapha- signs along with those of vāta are exposed fully and t disappear momentarily” (Ca.Sū. 17). The vātaja madhumeha caused by emaciation of tissues will have only vāta signs. Gadādhara holds that madhumeha is caused by only - āvṛtavāta (vāta that is covered or obstructed by other doṣas). As said by Carak, Vayu, when obstructed by the other dosas (and dusyas) carries the ojas - the essential immunity factor of the body and when brought to the urinary bladder, madhumeha, the incurable disease is manifested”. (Ca. Sū. 17). In the disease caused by the vata, aggravated due to excessive purifactory measures and emaciation of the tissues, there is no obstruction or covering of Vata by the other factors. 23-25. Reason for nomenclature of prameha as madhumeha Generally in all pramehas the individual passes urine that is sweet in taste and looks like honey and his body also gets sweetened, hence the name madhumeha is given to all these pramehas. 26. मधुकोशः तत्र दोषसंबन्धमाह-उदावर्तेत्यादि। उदावर्तरुजादाहैर्वातं, मोहतृड्दहनज्वरैः पित्तं, गौरवारुचिकाठिन्यैः कफं जानीयात् ॥ १८ ॥ यस्यान्त्रमन्नैरुपलेपिभिर्वा बालाश्मभिर्वा पिहितं यथावत् । संचीयते तस्य मलः सदोषः शनैः शनैः संकरवच्च नाड्याम्॥ १९॥ निरुध्यते तस्य गुदे पुरीषं निरेति कृच्छ्रादपि चाल्पमल्पम्। हन्नाभिमध्ये परिवृद्धिमेति तस्योदरं बद्धगुदं वदन्ति॥ २०॥ मधुकोशः बद्धगुदमाह-यस्यान्त्रमन्नैरित्यादि। उपलेपिभिः पिच्छिलैरन्नैः शाकशालूकादिभिः। पिहितं विवद्धम्। यथावदिति यथाईम्। मलः पुरीषम्। सदोष इति दोषत्रयसहितः। नाड्यामित्यन्त्रनाड्याम्। संकरबदिति संमार्जनीक्षिप्यमाणतृणाद्यवकरो यथा चीयते क्रमेण तथेत्यर्थः । बद्धगुदमिति गुद्दोपर्यन्त्रस्य बद्धत्वाद्वद्वगुदम्। यदुक्त चरके-‘पक्ष्मबालैः सहात्रेन भुक्तैर्बद्वायने गुदे’ (च.चि.अ. १३) इति। पुरीषायतनस्य रुद्धत्वात् प हन्नाभिमध्येऽन्नपाकस्थाने वृद्धिः, गुदमात्रनिरोधे तु मलदोषैर्गुदादूध्वमेवोदरवृद्धिः स्यात् ॥ १९–२० ॥ शल्यं तथाऽन्नोपहितं यदन्त्रं भुक्तं भिनत्त्यागतमन्यथा वा। तस्मात्स्वुतोऽन्त्रात्सलिलप्रकाशः स्रावः स्त्रवेद्वै गुदतस्तु भूयः॥ २१॥ नाभेरधश्चोदरमेति वृद्धिं निस्तुद्यते दाल्यति चातिमात्रमु। एतत्परिस्त्राव्युदरं प्रदिष्टं— ( सु.नि. ७ )
answer_text: Dosa relation is explained here. It is to be understood that vata is predominant when bloating of the abdomen, pain and flatulance are present; pitta, when delusion, thirst, burning sensation and fever are seen and kapha predominance is understood when heaviness, distaste and rigidity of the abdomen are t present. Signs and symptoms of Baddhagudodara When the intestines of an individual are obstructed by food stuffs that are very sticky or by small stones, then his faecal matter gets stuck and accumulates gradually as the slough in the drainage. Since the canal blocks its passage, very small quantity comes out with great difficulty. There will be swelling in the abdomi¬ nal part between the heart and navel. Such udara is called Baddha gudodara. 19-20. (Su. Ni 7). Upalepibhih means - by the food stuffs which are sticky in nature like roots of water lilly. Sadoşa means afflicted by the doşas. Sańkaravat means the obstruction is compared to that in a drainage by which gradual increase takes place in turbid waters. Baddha guda means constriction or obstruction of the intestines above the anal canal. In caraka, it is said, “The anal canal is obstructed by the quills and hairs that are eaten along with food". (Ca. Ci. 13). Since there is obtruction in the path way of faecal matter, there is swelling in the place of digestion i.e., the part between 4 M.N. Pt-II Mādhavanidānaṃ heart and navel. If the obstruction is only in the anus, then the swelling would be just above the anus. 19-20. Signs and symptoms of kṣatodara When a foreign body enters into the abdomen along with food and pierces. the intestines or by any other means, the intestines get perforated causing watery exudation which passes out from the anal canal repeatedly. There will be swelling in the abdomen in the region below the umbilicus. There will be pinning and tearing pain. This condition is also known as parisravyudara. 21. (Su. Ni. 7)
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 35, verse 21.

मधुकोशः मेदोजमाह-स्निग्ध इत्यादि। देहानुरूपक्षयवृद्धियुक्त इति देहक्षये क्षयं, देहवृद्धौ च वृद्धिं यातीत्यर्थः। गलेऽनुशब्दमिति अनुनादं करोति। ‘गले तु शब्दम्’–इति पाठान्तरं सुगमम्॥ ६॥ कृच्छ्राच्छ्वासन्तं मृदुसर्वगात्रं संवत्सरातीतमरोचकार्तम् ॥ ७॥ क्षीणं चं वैद्यो गलगण्डयुक्तं भिन्नस्वरं चापि विवर्जयेच्च। ( सु.नि. ११ ) मधुकोशः असाध्यतामाह-कृच्छ्राच्छ्वसन्तमित्यादि। कृच्छ्राच्छ्वसन्तं दुःखेन श्वास विमोक्षकारिणम्। भिन्नस्वरं स्वरभेदवन्तम् ॥ ७॥ कर्कन्धुकोलामलकप्रमाणैः कक्षांसमन्यागलवडक्षणेषु ॥ ८ ॥ मेदः कफाभ्यां चिरमन्दपाकैः स्याद्गण्डमाला बहुभिश्च गण्डैः । मधुकोशः स्थानंतुल्यतया गण्डमालामिहैवाह-कर्कन्धुकोलामलकप्रमाणैरित्यादि। कर्कन्धुः श्रृगालकोलिः, कोलं ब्रहद्वदरम्। मेदः कफाभ्यामिति मेदो दूष्यं, कफो दोषोऽत्रारम्भकः, मेदः कफौ प्राधान्येनोक्तौ; तेन वातपित्त- संबन्धोऽप्यत्र द्रष्टव्यः। यदाह भोजः, 'वातपित्तकफा वृद्धा मेदश्रापि समाचितम्। जङ्डयोः कण्डराः प्राप्य मत्स्याण्डसदृशान् बहून्॥ कुर्वन्ति ग्रथितांस्तेभ्यः पुनः प्रकुपितोऽनिलः। तान् दोषानूध्वंगो वक्षः- कक्षामन्या- गलाश्रितः ॥ नानाप्रकारान् कुरुते ग्रन्थीन् सा त्वपची स्मृता । तां तु मालाकृति विद्यात्कण्ठह्हद्दनुसन्धिषु ॥ गण्डमालां प विजानीयादपचीतुल्यलक्षणाम्’ इति । स्याद्गण्डमालेति मालातुल्यगण्डयोगाद्गण्डमाला। गलमात्र एव गण्डमाला चरके पठिता। यथा ‘मेदः कफाच्छोणितसंचयोत्थो गलस्य मध्ये गलगण्ड एकः । स्याद्रण्डमाला बहुभिश्च गण्डैः ’ ( च.चि.स्था. १२) इति ॥ ८ ॥ ते ग्रन्थयः केचिदवाप्तपाकाः स्त्रवन्ति नश्यन्ति भवन्ति चान्ये॥ ९॥ कालानुबन्धं चिरमादधाति सैवापचीति प्रवदन्ति तज्ज्ञाः। साध्याः स्मृताः पीनसपार्श्वशूलकासज्वरच्छर्दियुतास्त्वसाध्याः॥ १०॥ मधुकोशः गण्डमालातुल्यतयांऽपचीमाह–ते ग्रन्थय इत्यादि। ते इति गण्डमालारम्भक दोषदूष्यकृता ये ग्रन्थयस्त एवे– त्यर्थः। कालनुबन्धं चिरमिति चिरकालानुबन्धम्। सैवापचीति तादृशी अमालारूपा अपची भण्यते। सैवापचीति इतिशब्देनाभिहितत्वात् प्रवदन्तीति क्रियायोगेऽपि न द्वितीया। अपचीनिरुक्तिश्चापरापरोपचीयमानतया। अत एव 'चयप्रकर्षादपचीं वदन्ति' (सु.नि.स्था. ११) इति सुश्रुतः । चयप्रकर्षश्चा परापरभवनेनैव, साधुत्वं च नैरुक्तेन विधिना। यदुक्तम्-वर्णांगमो वर्णविपर्ययश्च द्वौ चापरौ वर्णविकारनाशौ। धातोस्तदर्थांतिशयेन योगस्तदुच्यते पञ्ठविधं निरुक्तम्’ इति। अत एवोक्त-नश्यन्ति भवन्ति चान्य इति। साध्याः स्मृता इति च्छेदः। पीनसादिभिरुप- द्रवैरसाध्याः अयं तु ग्रन्थिश्वरके गण्डमालायामस्ति; संग्रहकारेण तु गण्डमालया सह तुल्यत्वादपच्या अपच्यामेव पठितः ॥ ९–१० ॥ वातादयो मांसमसृक् प्रदुष्टाः संदूष्य मेदश्च तथा सिराश्च। ( सु.नि. ११) वृत्तोन्नतं विग्रथितं च शोथं कुर्वन्त्यतो ग्रन्थिरिति प्रदिष्टः ॥ ११ ॥
answer_text: In medoja galaganda, it is seen that the swelling increase when the body of the patient is repleted and it diseases when there is depletion in the patient. “gale tu sabdam” is different text which means sounds in the throat of the patient are heard. 6. Asādhyatā (incurability) of galaganda The physician should not take up the indiviual suffering from galaganda for treatment when he breathes with difficully, the whole body becomes soft, duration of the disease exceeds one year and he has a broken voice and emaciation. 7. (Su. Ni. 11) Galaganda-Gandamala Apaci-Granthy Arbuda Nidāna, 51 Kṛcchrāt śvɑsɑntɑṃ- those who breathe out with lot of difficulty. Bhinna svɑrɑm - Those who have disturbed or broken voice. 7. Picture of gandamālā Due to vitiated meda and kapha a number of gandas (morbid growths) occur in the arm pit, on the scapular region, neck, throat and the groin region in the size of karkandhu (small ziziphus furit) kola (ordinary ziziphus furit) and āmalakī (goose-berry) which ripen slowly after long time of onset, are called gandamala. 8. (Su. Ni. 11) Since the place of origin is same gandamāla is also explained here. Karkandhu is small variety of ziziphus fruit while kola is big variety of the same fruit. Meda (fat) is the dūṣya (vitiated) and kapha is the vitiator or the initiating factor. These two are said to be predominant factor. The role of vāta and pitta is also to be considered here. As said by Bhoja, “The increased vata, pitta and kapha and also the accumu¬ lated fat take shelter in the muscles of the groins and cause many knot-like forms that look like egg of fish. Vata which is aggravated by them, in turn-takes these morbid factors to chest, arm-pits and neck and causes various types of knots in those places which are called apacī. These look like garlands in joints of neck, heart/chest and jaw. In these places, they are called gandamālā.” Since they look like garland in the ganda (root of the cheeks) there called gandamala (cheek- garland). As per Caraka, gandamālā occurs only in the cheeks— “galaganda is one lump that occurs in the centre of the neck due to meda vitiated by kapha and accumulation of blood; and it is called gandamala when many lumps occur.". 8. (Ca. Ci. 12) Mādhavanidānaṃ Characteristics of Apaci Those tumour like swellings get ripened, exudate the slough and get supressed and some others originate in the near viscinity. In this way this disease continues to last long. This is called apaci according to the specialist plysicians, This disease is curable but it becomes incurable when associated with coryza, pain in the flanks, cough, fever and vomitting. 9, 10. Apac is detailed here after gandamala since there is similarity (in size?) among these two types of disease. Those - means those tumour like swellings which are caused by the same dosa and dūsya that give rise to gandamālā. Continuos means they keep rising, supressing and again rising continuously. It is called apaci because it keeps coming out or increasing one from another “aparāparopad̃yamānatayā” Suśruta, therfore, said, “Cayaprakarṣūdapacīm vadanti” it is called apacī because it keeps growing abundantly". (Su. ni. 11). Cayaprakarsa (abundantly increasing) is by arising one after another ( aparaparabhavana ) this nirukti is acceptable. As said, Varnāgama, varna viparyaya, varna vikāra, varna nāsa, Arthātiśayayoga are the five types of Nirukti (definition). That is why it is said that in appa the tumours get dessroyed and keep originating (Naśyanti bhavanti cānya). This disease becomes incurable when associated with complications like coryza etc, . This type of tumour is described in gaṇḍamāla in caraka. But here apaci is mentioned seperately. Charecteristics of granthi Galaganda-Gandamala Apaci-Granthy Arbuda Nidāna The aggravated Tridosas vitiate mamsa (muscle-tissue) Asrk (blood) meda (fat) and sirā (blood vessals-veins?) and cause swelling which is round in shape big in size and hard for touch that looks solidified which is why it is called granthi (tu¬ mour). 11. (Su. Ni. 11)
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 38, verse 11.

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidanam (Part 2) (Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 39, verse 6):

मधुकोशः श्लीपदेषु कफस्याव्यभिंचारेण प्राधान्यमाह-त्रीण्यप्येतानीत्यादि। ननु, यद्यव्यभिचारी सर्वत्र कफः कथं तर्ह्यकदोषजत्वव्यपदेशः सर्वस्य द्विदोषजत्वप्रसङ्गात्? उच्यते, अनुबन्धोऽत्र कफः, न त्वनुबन्ध्यः, एतेनात्र न द्विदोषजप्रसङ्ग इत्यभिप्रायः॥ ५॥ पुराणोदकभूयिष्ठाः सर्वतुषु च शीतलाः । ये देशास्तेषु जायन्ते श्लीपदानि विशेषतः ॥ ६ ॥
answer_text: Kapha is considered as having definite role in slipada. Then why has the dual¬ dosa type of this disease been not mentioned here, whereas in many places the diseases are categorised as per dvidosaja predominance? It is said in the answer to this question that kapha is considered here as anubandha —associate factor and not anubandhya - main factor which is why the dvidoşa type of categorisation has not been given in this disease 5. The places where incidence of Stipada is common In the places where stagnant water is abundant and temperature is low in all seasons, more incidence of Stipada, specially, is seen. 6. (Su. Ni. 12)
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 39, verse 6.

मधुकोशः कफजमाह-शरावेत्यादि। शरावसद्रश इति महत्त्वसूचनपरम्॥ ६॥ तनुपीतसिताश्चैषामास्त्रावः क्रमशः स्मृताः । मधुकोशः पाकानन्तरं संभूतास्त्रावलिङ्गमाह-तनुपीतसिताश्चैषामित्यादि। क्रमश इति यथाक्रमं; तेन वातेन तनुः, पित्तेन पीतः, कफेन सितः, तनुस्त्रावे वातानुरूपो वर्णो ज़ेयः॥ नानावर्णरुजास्त्रावो घाटालो विषमो महान्॥ ७॥ विषमं पच्यते चापि विद्रधिः सान्निपातिकः। ( सु.नि. ९ ) मधुकोशः सन्निपातजमाह-नानेत्यादि। नानावर्णरुजास्त्राव इति नानाशब्दः प्रत्येकमभिसंबध्यते, नाना बहुविधा वर्णाः कृष्णपीतशुक्लवर्णाः, रुजास्तोददाहकण्ड्वादिकाः, तनुपीतसिता आस्रावाश्च यस्य स तथा । अन्यत्र शोथे पाककाले नानारूजा, अत्र तु सर्वदा। घाटाल इति घाटा अस्यास्ति स घाटाला इति मत्वर्थीयो लच्, अत्युच्छि्ताग्रत्वेन घाटाल इव। विषमोऽसाध्यत्वात्। विषमं पच्यत इति चिराचिरगम्भीरोत्तानोर्ध्वानूर्ध्वभेदेन विषमं यथा भवति तथा पच्यत इति विषमसमम्। ननु, विषमपाकित्वं वातिके विद्रधावुक्तं, तथाऽनुपक्रान्ते च शोथे; यथा- योऽभ्युत्थितोऽत्यो यदि वा महान् स्यात् क्रियां विना पाकमुपैति शोथः । विशालमूलो विषमो विदग्धः स कृच्छूतां यात्यवगाढदोषः' (सु.सू.अ. १७) इति; अतः संशये कथं मिथो भेदप्रतीतिः ? उच्यते, वातिकेऽप्रतीकारेणैव विषमपाकित्वम्, इह पुनः प्रतीकारेऽपि वैषम्यं; वातिके तु पाकमात्रवैषम्यं, न तु गाम्भीर्यादिना, अतो वातिकः साध्यः ॥ ७ ॥ तैस्तैर्भावैरभिहते क्षते वाऽपथ्यकारिणः ॥ ८॥ क्षतोष्मा वायुविसृतः सरक्तं पित्तमीरयेत्। ज्वरस्तृष्णा च दाहश्व जायते तस्य देहिनः॥ ९॥ आगन्तुर्विद्रधिर्ह्येष पित्तविद्रधिलक्षणः । ( सु.नि. ९ )

Nature of discharge in relation with dosas The discharge is thin in vata type of vidradhi; it is yellowish in pitta type and whitish in kapha type of vidradhi. Thin, yellow and white are the nature of exudation in the vidradhi after they ripen and open. Colours are given in the case of pitta and kapha. But consistency is mentioned in vāta type. The colour is to be understood as in relation to vāta, i.e., black or red. Sannipāta type of vidradhi The sannipata type of vidradhi is associated with various colour, pain exuda¬ tion; looks like the ghātā (the high rising preceding part of the neck on the back of an ox); irregular in size and ripening style and veyr big in size. 7. (Su. Ni. 9). Various' applies to colours, pain and exudation also. Colours - white, yellow and black; pains - pinning sensation, burning sensation, pruritus etc., exudations - thin, yellow and white. In other varieties of swellings, various types of pains are seen during pākakāla (ripening stage) but here, these are present all through the Vidradhi Nidāna course of disease. It is compared to ghāṭā - high raising structure like the back of the ox. Irregularity is due to incurability. Irregularity in ripening is in accordance with the time taken for outset less or more, deep rooted or superficial and highly swollen or slightly swollen conditions. Irregular ripening is seen in vata vidradhi and also in sotha which is not treated— “Either small or big on onset, Sotha does ripen without treatment. The big based, irregular shaped and over burnt becomes tough due to ill rooting.” (Su. Su 17). In such doubtful condition how can there be contradicting statements? It said in the answer that the irregularity in ripening of Vatavidradhi results by not treating it but here the treatment has no effect on the ripening pattern. In vatavidradhi irregularity is limited to ripening alone but not the deep rootedness etc., which is why vatika type of vidradhi is curable. 7. Vidradhi caused by external stimuli Having hit by sticks and or stones, weapons etc., if the individual indulges in incompatiable foods and behaviour aspects, the warmth of the injury gets pro¬ voked by vāta and disturbs pitta along with rakta, causing fever, thirst and burning sensation to him. This is called Agantujā vidradhi. Its symptomatology is similar to that of pitta vidradhi. 8, 9. (Su. Ni. 9)

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidanam (Part 2) (Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 41, verse 13):

एकदेशोत्थितः शोथो व्रणानां पूर्वलक्षणम्। षड्विधः स्यात् पृथक्सर्वरक्तागन्तुनिमित्तजः॥ १॥ शोथाः षडेते विज्ञेयाः प्रापुक्कैः शोथलक्षणैः। विशेषः कथ्यते चैषां पक्रापक्रादिनिश्चये॥ २॥ मधुकोशः प्रायेण चिकित्सासाधर्म्यात् भाविव्रणत्वसंबन्धतुल्यत्वाच्च व्रणशोथनिदानमाह एकदेशोत्थित इत्यादि। षड्विध इति संख्याकथनं द्वन्द्वजनिषेधार्थम्। प्रागुक्तैरिति आम-पक्रैषणीयोक्तैः, तत्र हि 'वातश्चयथुररूणः कृष्णो वा परुषो मृदुरनवस्थितः’ (सु.सू. १७) इत्यादिना षट् शोथलक्षणान्युक्तानि। विशेषः कथ्यते चैषमिति तत्रानुक्तो विशेषः कथ्यत इत्यर्थः। पक्वापक्वादिनिश्चय इति। अत्रादिशब्देन पच्यमानस्य परिग्रहः॥ १–२॥ विषमं पच्यते वातात् पित्तोत्थश्राचिराच्चिरम्। कफजः पित्तवच्छोथो रक्तागन्तुसमुद्भवः॥ ३॥ मधुकोशः वातादिभेदेन विशेषलक्षणमाह-विषममित्यादि। पित्तवदिति पित्तशोथवदचिरं पच्यते ॥ ३ ॥ मन्दोष्मताऽल्पशोथत्वं काठिन्यं त्वक्सवर्णता। मन्दवेदनता चैतच्छोथानामामलक्षणम्॥ ४॥ दह्यते दहनेनेव क्षारेणेव च पच्यते। पिपीलिकागणेनेव दश्यते छिद्यते तथा॥ ५॥ भिद्यते चैव शस्त्रेण दण्डेनेव च ताड्यते। पीड्यते पाणिनेवान्तः सूचीभिरिव तुद्यते॥ ६॥ सोषायोषो विवर्णः स्यादङ्कल्येवावघट्यते। आसने शयने स्थाने शान्तिं वृश्चिकविद्धवत् ॥ ७॥ न गच्छेदाततः शोथो भवेदाघ्मातबस्तिवत्। ज्वरस्तृष्णाऽरुचिश्चैव पच्यमानस्य लक्षणम्॥ ८॥ मधुकोशः पच्यमानलक्षणमाह-दह्यत इत्यादि। पच्यमानशोथे पित्तलिङ्गान्येव भूयसा भवन्ति, विदाहस्य पित्तप्रकोप- जत्वात्; विदाहश्चात्र दोषादीनामेव। तेनज्वरतृष्णारुच्यादयोऽत्र पित्तलिङ्गानि। छिद्यत इति द्विधा क्रियत इव। भिद्यत इति विदार्यते। सोषाचोष इति उषा दाहः, चोषः पार्श्वस्थाग्निसंतापवद् व्यथा, ताभ्यां सह वर्तते यः स तथा ॥ ५-८ ॥ वेदनोपशमः शोथोऽलोहितोऽल्पो न चोन्नतः। प्रादुर्भावो वलीनां च तोदः कण्डूर्मुहर्मुंहः॥ ९॥ उपद्रवाणां प्रशमो निम्नता स्फुटनं त्वचाम्। बस्ताविवाम्बुसंचारः स्याच्छोथेऽङ्गलिपीडिते॥ १०॥ पूयस्य पीडयत्येकमन्तमन्ते च पीडिते। भक्ताकाड्क्षा भवेच्चैतच्छोथानां पक्वलक्षणम्॥ ११॥ मधुकोशः पक्रलक्षणमाह-वेदनोपशम इत्यादि। दाहादिवेदनोपशान्तिः, विदाहोपशमेन पित्तस्याबलवत्त्वात्। तोदः कण्ड्रश्चात्र व वातकफलिङ्डम् । प्रादुर्भावो वलीनामिति मांसशैथिल्याद्वलीसंभवः। उपद्रवाणां प्रशम इति पित्तकोपजनिता उषाचोषतृष्णारुच्यादयो रोगा एव उपद्रवास्तेषां प्रशमः निम्नता स्वरूपतः, अङ्गलिपीडनाद्वा। स्फूटनं त्वचामितिं किंचित्त्वगवद्रणम्। बस्ताविवेत्यादि। बस्तिश्चर्मपुटकं, पूयस्येत्यत्र ‘संचार’ इति शेषः अयमर्थः- बस्तौ यथाऽम्बुसंचारस्तथा शोथेऽङ्गलिपीडिते सति पूयस्य संचारः पीडयत्येकमन्तमन्ते च पीडित इति एकमन्ते देशम, अन्ते अवयवे पीडिते पीडयत्यवगाहते, ‘पूय’ इति शेषः॥ ९-११ ॥ नर्तेऽनिलाद्वड्न विना च पित्तं पाकः कफं चापि विना न पूयः। तस्माद्धि सर्वान् परिपाककाले पचन्ति शोथांस्त्रय एव दोषाः ॥ १२॥ मधुकोशः एकदोषारब्धेऽपि शोथे पाककाले सर्वदोषसंबन्धमाह-नर्तेऽनिलाद्रुगित्यादि। रुग्रुजा तोदादिरूपा। सुश्रुते, त्रिभिरेतैः शोणितचतुर्थेश्व शरीरमिदं धार्यते' (सु.सू.स्था. २१) इति द्वितीयदर्शने शोणितप्राधान्याख्याप- ( कमाश्रित्योक्तम्-'.कालान्तरेणाभ्युदितं तु पित्तं कृत्वा वशे वातकफौ प्रसह्य। पचत्यतः शोणितमेष पाको मतः परेषां विदृषां द्वितीयः' (सु.सू.स्था. १७) इति। अत्र दर्शने पित्तं विदाहकुपितं शोणितं दूष्यं कर्मभूतं पचति, वातकफौ वशे कृत्वा क्रोडीकृत्य, हीनार्थो वा वशेशब्दः, वातकफौ हीनौ कृत्वेत्यर्थः; शोणितं कर्तभूतं वा, तेन पक्त्यनुकूलत्वाद्विवक्षितं; पूर्वदर्शने कफात् पूयः, अत्र दर्शने शोणितात् पूय इति विशेषः। गम्भीरपाके शोथे सकलामपच्यमानलक्षणानुदयादज्ञायमाने लक्षणान्तरमुक्त सुश्रुतेन। तद्यथा-'कफजेषु खलु शोथेषु गम्भीरगति- त्वादभिघातजेष् वा केषुचिदसमस्तं पक्रलक्षणं दृष्टवा पक्रमपक्रमिति भिषङ्मोहमुपैति, यत्र हि त्वक्सवर्णता शीतशोथताऽल्परुजताऽश्मवद्धनता च, न तत्र मोहमुपेयात्' (सु.सू.स्था. १७) इति । अस्यार्थः-यदारागदा- हादिवेदनासमुदयानन्तरं त्वक्सवर्णतादिनि भवन्ति तेदा न मोहमज्ञानतामुपेयात् पक्रमेवेति निश्चिनुयात्। गदाधरेण तु त्वक्सवर्णतादीनि संशयहेतू-युक्तानि; यतस्तेन 'गम्भीरपाकित्वादन्तः पाको बहिः पुनस्त्वक्सावर्ण्यं, गम्भीरपाकित्वादेव बहिः शीतता, कफारब्धत्वान्मन्दरुजताऽश्मवच्च घनता'-इत्यभिधाय 'शेषंपक्रलक्षणणैजा- नीयात्’-इत्युक्तम्॥ १२॥ कक्षं समासाद्य यथैव वह्निर्वाय्वीरितः सन्दहति प्रसह्य। ( सु.सू. १७ ) तथैव पूयो ह्यविनिःसृतो हि मांसं सिराः स्नायु च खादतीह॥ १३॥
answer_text: The inflammation that occurs in a particular area is considered as a premonitary symptom of an wound. This of six types viz., three due to each of the three doşas individually, one due to all of them, one due to rakta and one due to sudden cause. They have the same type of symptomatology as that of Sotha which are envisaged earlier. The specific features to determine the ripening or unripe condition are being explained (in the following stanzas). 1, 2. Since there is probable similarity of management and possibility of turning into a wound in the future, (like the vidradhi), vrana śotha (inflammation that precedes wound)is being told. Saying that “it is of six types” is to negate the existance of dual dosa affliction (in this disease). “Envisaged earliear” means explained in the “āmapakvaiṣanīya” chapter, as “vāta svayathu (vāta type of Śotha) is red or black in colour, rough surfaced, smooth for grip and not strong based” (Su. Su. 17) etc., six types of Sotha has been featured. “Visesa” means whatever is not mentioned there and relevant, will be added here. “Pakvūpakvādi - ripened, unripe etc., - here the word ādi (etc., ) indicates pacyamāna (ripening) stage also. 1-2, The specific ripening nature of inflammation as per the dosa The ripening takes place irregularly in vata type of vraṇa śotha. It occurs fast in pitta type and it is delayed in kapha type of vrana śothà. In rakta (blood) and āgantu (sudden) originated types the ripening takes place (fast), as in the case of pittaja vraṇaśotha. 3. Vranasotha Nidāna Signs and symptoms during āma & pacyamāna (unripe & ripening) stages of vranaśotha Mild heat and inflammation, hardness having same colour as that of the skin and mild pain are the features of āma (unripe) vraṇa śotha. During the pacyamāna (ripening) stage, it feels as if being burnt by fire, being ripened forcibly by applying alkalies, being bitten by many ants, being cut, being opened by weapons, being hit by stick, being squeezed with hands and being pierced with needles. There is burning and feeling of heat on the inflammed area, discolouration and also feeling of manipulation with fingers. There is no relief even on sitting, lying down or standing as in the case of scorpion-sting. The swelling looks like the bloated bladder and the individual has fever, thirst and distaste during this stage. 4-8. When the inflammation ripens, pitta symptoms are seen predominantly dur¬ ing that ripening stage because the baking takes place due to aggravation of pitta. The baking or ripening occurs in the morbid factors only. Fever, thirst, distaste etc., are only the features of pitta. Chidyate means seperating into two. Bhidyate means breaking. uṣa is burning sensation and coṣa means feeling of being exposed to fire kept close to the abcess. These two are experienced together in this stage. 4-8. Features of pakvāvasthā (ripened stage) of vraṇa śotha (inflammation) Mādhavanidānaṃ The suffering is diminished, inflammation looses the red colour, becomes depleted, and not high rising, formation of wrinkles, pinning sensation, repeated itching sensation, palliation of complications, sunken appearance and loss of elas¬ ticity and striation of the skin, shifting of liquids in the swollen part on pressing with fingers as the water shifts in the leather bag, on pressing from one side to another and there is urge for eating food in the individual - when the inflamma¬ tion ripen. 9-11. Due to diminishing of pitta - burning etc., also palliate; pinning sensation and itching are the featrues of vāta-kapha. The wrinkle formation is due to loss of tone in the muscle. The complications are burning sensation etc., which are also palli¬ ated. The sunkenness is in appearance or it may be considered as pitting nature of the swelling. Breaking of the skin is formation of striations in the skin. 9-11. Role of all three dosas during ripening There is no pain without vata, no ripening without pitta and no pus formation without kapha. Therefore, all three dosas involve in the ripening of all the inflammations/swellings. 12. (Su. Su. 17). Vraṇaśotha Nidāna The relation of all three dosas during paka kala (ripening stage) even in the sotha caused by single dosa is being explained here. Ruk is pain in the form of pinning sensation etc. Considering the statement of Suśruta, “These three and the fourth one, rakta are the supporting factors of śarīra (body)", (Su. Sū 21) thūs considering rakta as a predominant factor it is again mentioned by Susruta, “In due course of time, pitta becomes prominent, gets the vāta and kapha under control, and bakes the rakta. This ripening is considered as secondary by the scholars (Su. Su. 17). In the beginning kapha is considered as transforming into pus but as per the above statement, it is blood that turns to pus. Susruta gives some more features in the case of deep ripening of vraṇa śotha since the ama and pacyanāma features are not explicit. “In the kapha śotha and abhighātaja (traumatic) śotha, looking at the incomplete pakva (ripened) symptoms the physician is often confused whether it is ripened or not; where colour of the swollen area is like that of the skin, when the pain is less and the inflammation is rock-solid there need not be any doubt" i.e. when burning sensation etc.; are palliated and skin colour is attained on the swelling then, one need not doubt and can determine that it has ripened. Gadadhara says that attainment of skin colour is a symptom to be doubted. He states, when the paka - ripening take inside, the external skin-colour looks equal to that of remaining skin, the external touch will be cold and due to kapha being the predominant factor, there is less pain and rock-solid condition”. After saying so, he adds that the remaining condition is to be known by symptoms of ripened condi¬ tion. 12. Complications caused by not draining the pus As the fire burns the whole heap of grass with the help of vayu (wind), in the same way the pus which is not drained out, eats away the muscle, veins and the ligaments. 13. (Su. Sū 17)

विदाहश्चात्र दोषादीनामेव। तेनज्वरतृष्णारुच्यादयोऽत्र पित्तलिङ्गानि। छिद्यत इति द्विधा क्रियत इव। भिद्यत इति विदार्यते। सोषाचोष इति उषा दाहः, चोषः पार्श्वस्थाग्निसंतापवद् व्यथा, ताभ्यां सह वर्तते यः स तथा ॥ ५-८ ॥ वेदनोपशमः शोथोऽलोहितोऽल्पो न चोन्नतः। प्रादुर्भावो वलीनां च तोदः कण्डूर्मुहर्मुंहः॥ ९॥ उपद्रवाणां प्रशमो निम्नता स्फुटनं त्वचाम्। बस्ताविवाम्बुसंचारः स्याच्छोथेऽङ्गलिपीडिते॥ १०॥ पूयस्य पीडयत्येकमन्तमन्ते च पीडिते। भक्ताकाड्क्षा भवेच्चैतच्छोथानां पक्वलक्षणम्॥ ११॥ मधुकोशः पक्रलक्षणमाह-वेदनोपशम इत्यादि। दाहादिवेदनोपशान्तिः, विदाहोपशमेन पित्तस्याबलवत्त्वात्। तोदः कण्ड्रश्चात्र व वातकफलिङ्डम् । प्रादुर्भावो वलीनामिति मांसशैथिल्याद्वलीसंभवः। उपद्रवाणां प्रशम इति पित्तकोपजनिता उषाचोषतृष्णारुच्यादयो रोगा एव उपद्रवास्तेषां प्रशमः निम्नता स्वरूपतः, अङ्गलिपीडनाद्वा। स्फूटनं त्वचामितिं किंचित्त्वगवद्रणम्। बस्ताविवेत्यादि। बस्तिश्चर्मपुटकं, पूयस्येत्यत्र ‘संचार’ इति शेषः अयमर्थः- बस्तौ यथाऽम्बुसंचारस्तथा शोथेऽङ्गलिपीडिते सति पूयस्य संचारः पीडयत्येकमन्तमन्ते च पीडित इति एकमन्ते देशम, अन्ते अवयवे पीडिते पीडयत्यवगाहते, ‘पूय’ इति शेषः॥ ९-११ ॥ नर्तेऽनिलाद्वड्न विना च पित्तं पाकः कफं चापि विना न पूयः। तस्माद्धि सर्वान् परिपाककाले पचन्ति शोथांस्त्रय एव दोषाः ॥ १२॥ मधुकोशः एकदोषारब्धेऽपि शोथे पाककाले सर्वदोषसंबन्धमाह-नर्तेऽनिलाद्रुगित्यादि। रुग्रुजा तोदादिरूपा। सुश्रुते, त्रिभिरेतैः शोणितचतुर्थेश्व शरीरमिदं धार्यते' (सु.सू.स्था. २१) इति द्वितीयदर्शने शोणितप्राधान्याख्याप- ( कमाश्रित्योक्तम्-'.कालान्तरेणाभ्युदितं तु पित्तं कृत्वा वशे वातकफौ प्रसह्य। पचत्यतः शोणितमेष पाको मतः परेषां विदृषां द्वितीयः' (सु.सू.स्था. १७) इति। अत्र दर्शने पित्तं विदाहकुपितं शोणितं दूष्यं कर्मभूतं पचति, वातकफौ वशे कृत्वा क्रोडीकृत्य, हीनार्थो वा वशेशब्दः, वातकफौ हीनौ कृत्वेत्यर्थः; शोणितं कर्तभूतं वा, तेन पक्त्यनुकूलत्वाद्विवक्षितं; पूर्वदर्शने कफात् पूयः, अत्र दर्शने शोणितात् पूय इति विशेषः। गम्भीरपाके शोथे सकलामपच्यमानलक्षणानुदयादज्ञायमाने लक्षणान्तरमुक्त सुश्रुतेन। तद्यथा-'कफजेषु खलु शोथेषु गम्भीरगति- त्वादभिघातजेष् वा केषुचिदसमस्तं पक्रलक्षणं दृष्टवा पक्रमपक्रमिति भिषङ्मोहमुपैति, यत्र हि त्वक्सवर्णता शीतशोथताऽल्परुजताऽश्मवद्धनता च, न तत्र मोहमुपेयात्' (सु.सू.स्था. १७) इति । अस्यार्थः-यदारागदा- हादिवेदनासमुदयानन्तरं त्वक्सवर्णतादिनि भवन्ति तेदा न मोहमज्ञानतामुपेयात् पक्रमेवेति निश्चिनुयात्। गदाधरेण तु त्वक्सवर्णतादीनि संशयहेतू-युक्तानि; यतस्तेन 'गम्भीरपाकित्वादन्तः पाको बहिः पुनस्त्वक्सावर्ण्यं, गम्भीरपाकित्वादेव बहिः शीतता, कफारब्धत्वान्मन्दरुजताऽश्मवच्च घनता'-इत्यभिधाय 'शेषंपक्रलक्षणणैजा- नीयात्’-इत्युक्तम्॥ १२॥ कक्षं समासाद्य यथैव वह्निर्वाय्वीरितः सन्दहति प्रसह्य। ( सु.सू. १७ ) तथैव पूयो ह्यविनिःसृतो हि मांसं सिराः स्नायु च खादतीह॥ १३॥

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidanam (Part 2) (Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 44):

मधुकोशः कष्टसाध्यतामाह-अल्पेत्यादि। वातात्मकस्येति। वातप्रकृतेः । उपद्रवैरिति। उपद्रवा ज्वराध्मानमूत्रपुरीष- सङ्गादयः ॥ ८ ॥ भिन्नं कपाल कट्यां तु सन्धिमुक्तं तथा च्युतम्। जघनं प्रतिपिष्टं च वर्जयेद्धि विचक्षणः॥ ९॥ असंश्लिष्टकपाल च ललाटे चूर्णित च यत्। भग्न स्तनान्तरे पृष्ठे शङ्वे मूर्धि च वर्जयेत्॥ १०॥ मधुकोशः असाध्यतमाह-भिन्नं कपालमित्यादि। भग्नमिति वाच्ये भिन्नमिति यत् कृतं तत् कपालानां प्रायशो भेदात्। अत एवोक्त -'कपालानि विभज्यन्ते' (सु.शा.अ. ५) इति। नुन, कट्यस्थ्नः कपालसंज्ञाया अभावात् कथमुच्यते भिन्न कपाल कट्यामिति ? यदुक्त सुश्रते-‘जानुनितम्बांसगण्डतालुश्रह्ववङ्क्षणशिरः सु कपालानि’ (सु.शा.अ. ५) इति; उच्यते, नितम्बग्रहणेन तत्र कटीग्रहणाददोषः; अथवा सर्वं कपालसंज्ञितमस्थि - भिन्नं, तथा कट्यां चास्थिभिन्न वर्जयेत्। असंश्लिष्टकपाल चेति तु नियमार्थं; तेन ललाटे कपालस्यासंश्लिष्टस्यासाध्यत्वं, नान्यथा भिन्नस्येति। भिन्न कपालमिति काण्डभग्नमेतत्। सन्धिमुक्तमिति नानाविधमपि सन्धिमुक्त कट्यां न सिध्यतीति। च्युतमिति अधः क्षिप्त, अन्यस्तु विश्लिष्टमाह; अथवा कट्यां सन्धिमुक्त युतलक्षणं न सर्वम्। जघनं प्रतिपिष्ट चेति जघनस्थाने पिष्टमुत्पिष्टमेतत्तथा च्युतामिति चे। संधिमुक्तं पुनविशेषार्थमुक्त, विशेषाभिथानादन्यस्य कटीसन्थिमुक्तस्य कदाचित् साध्यता सूच्यते, अत एव चिकित्सिते ‘ततः स्थानस्थिते सन्धौ’ (सु.चि.अ ३) इति वक्ष्यति। असंश्लिष्टकपालं च ललाटे चूर्णितं च [ यदिति यथा अविद्यमानसंश्लेषं यत् कपालं, तथा ललाटे ] चूर्णितं च यत् विघटितसन्धि तदसाध्यम्। भग्नमिति सामान्येन सन्धिमुक्त काण्डभग्न गृह्यते। अन्ये तु भग्नमित्यनेन काण्डभग्नविशेष ‘प्रसारणे कप्ममानम्’ इत्यनेनोक्त’ वदन्ति। उक्त’ च भालुकिना-‘शह्व’ मुध्रिन स्तनात्तरे वा काण्डेभग्न मरणाय’ इति। स्तनान्तरे उरसि, मूर्धिन चूडास्थाने॥ ९-१०॥ सम्यक् सन्धितमप्यस्थि दुर्निक्षेपनिबन्धनात् । संक्षोभाद्वाऽपि यद्रच्छेद्विक्रियां तच्च वर्जयेत् ॥ ११ ॥ ( सु.नि. १५ ) मधुकोशः सर्वेषामनवधानतोऽसाध्यत्वमाह–सम्यगित्यादि। सन्धितं संयमितम्। दुनिक्षेपनिबन्धनादिति दुःस्थापनात्तथा दुष्टबन्धनात्। संक्षोभाद्वेति अभिघातभयादिसंक्षोभात्। अयमर्थः-सम्यक् संयमितमपि दुःस्थापनात्, सुन्यस्तमपि दुष्टबन्धनात्, सुन्यस्तं सुबद्धमपि संक्षोभाद्विकृतमसाध्यम् ॥ ११ ॥ तरुणास्थीनि नम्यन्ते भिद्यन्ते नलकानि च। कपालानि विभज्यन्ते स्फुटन्ति रुचकानि च॥ १२॥ ( सु.नि. १५ ) इति श्रीमाधवकरविरचिते माधवनिदाने भग्ननिदानं समाप्तम्॥ ४४॥ मधुकोशः अस्थिविशेषे भग्नविशेषमाह-तरुणास्थीनीत्यादि। नम्यन्ते वक्रलक्षणं भग्नम्। घ्राणकर्णाक्षिपुटेषु तरुणं कोमलमस्थि। भिद्यन्ते नलकानि चेति अस्थ्यन्तरानुप्रवेशाद्भिद्यन्ते अतिपातितलक्षणेन च भग्नेन नलकानि युज्यन्ते; अन्ये तु द्वादशविधमपि भग्नमत्रेच्छन्ति। कपालानि विभज्यन्त इति कापलेषु विदरणलक्षणो भङ्क । ‘विभिद्यन्ते’ इति पाठान्तरम्, अर्थस्तु स एव। रुचकानि दन्ताः, तेषु स्फुटितलक्षणो भड़्गः । अस्थीनि पञ्चविधानि तरुणनलकपालवलयरुचकभेदात्। रुचकानि चेति चकाराद्वलयान्यपि स्फुटितानि भवन्तीति । एतत सुश्रुते स्फुटितं भग्नम्॥ १.२ ॥ इति श्रीकण्ठदत्तकृतायां मधुकोशव्याख्यायां भग्ननिदानं समाऩम्॥ ४४॥
answer_text: Vatatmaka means the one who has vata prakrti (Vata-temperament). complications of fracture are fever, bloating of the abdomen and constipation of urine and faeces etc.. 8. (Anātmavataḥ-the one who does not know about himself - this quality leads to improper intake of diet—Atankadarpana) Bhagna Nidāna Asadhyatā (Incurability of fracture) When the fractures occur in the flat bone (of the skull), pelvic bone in the form of dislocation of the joint or downward displacement and dislocation of the joint are not to be treated. Dislocated fracture in the skull and multiple fracture on the fore-head and also fracture at the mediastinum, vertebra, temple bone and on the top of the fore-head are also to be discarded from treating. 9-10. (Su. Ni. 15). When the word “Bhagna” is to be used in the case of bone-shaft breakage, the usage of the word, “Bhinna” is used, to denote the difference of the shape of the kapalūsthi (flat bone) with the other longitudinal bones etc.. That is why it is said that the flat bones get seperated. Su. Ni. 15. when “Kaṭi Asthi” is not given the term kapalāsthi (flat bone), how can it be possible to apply the word bhinna to katyasthi (flat bone)? It is told in Susruta “In the knees, buttocks, scapular region, cheeks, palate, temple, groins and head, the bones are flat.” Here the buttock can be taken as the place of pelvic bone. Hence there is no mistake in the above statement. Otherwise it can also be taken as “Asamslista kapala” (dislocated/detached flatbone) is a pre-requisite for incurability, because only detached flat bone in the fracture of fore-head is incurable not all other fractures. Bhinnam kapalam is fracture of the flat bone. Sandhimuktā dislocation of the joint, though is of many types, does not apply to the pelvic bone. Cyuta means Adhahksipta (down-ward displacement). The pratipista type of fracture also in the jaghana (pubic) regions means Mādhavanidānaṃ along with other, pista, utpista types. Sandhimukta is specifically mentioned to exempt the Sandhimukta in kaṭisandhi from incurability; as will be told, “in cases of fracture in the joints and still the bone is kept in place” - (Su.Ci 3). The incurability is applicable to the detached flat bone and also to the comminuted fracture of the fore head. The word bhagna is taken as both Sandhimukta and Kāṇḍa bhagna. Others interpret “bhagna” as breakage of temple bone, skull and mediastenum that leads to death. Stanāntare in between the nipple points/breasts, means - in the chest. Mūrdhni means in the top of the fore-head. 9-10. General incurability due to improper management – Inspite of proper placing of the bone, if it is bandaged displacing it or by shaking or disturbing, that goes irregular. Such condition is also to be left without treating (since such condition is incurable). 11. (Su. Ni. 15). Sandhitam" means set properly; Durniksepanibandhanat means improperly set and improperly bandaged. Sanksobhat disturbed or shaken due to fear of injury. In short, though the fracture is set properly, due to improper alignment; properly aligned also due to bad bandage; even the properly placed and properly ban¬ daged-due to disturbance it becomes deformed which is incurable. 11. Nature of fracture - based on the nature of the bone The cartilages bend, the long bones break, the flat bones seperate or show cracks and the teeth break up into pieces on getting injured. 12. (Su. Ni 15). Thus ends chapter on fracture in Mādhava’s book on diagnosis written by Srīmādhavakara. 44. Bhagna, Nidāna Namyante - bent down. This occurs to the cartilages in the nose, ears and eyes. The breakage affects the inner bone, also in the fracture occuring to the long bones. Some say all the twelve varieties of fractures occurs to the long bones (as per the injury?) The seperation or cracking takes place in the flat bones. Some read, Vibhidyante" in the place of Vibhajyante which also means the same. Rucaka means teeth which break up into pieces. The bones are of five types viz, Taruna (cartilage), Nalaka ( long bones), Kapāla (Flat-bones), Valaya (ribs) and Rucaka (teeth); by using the letter ca in Rucakāni cā it should be taken that the valaya (ribs) also seperate into pieces on injury. Sphutana is taken as Bhagna in Susruta. 12. Thus ends the chapter on Bhagnanidana (Diagnosis of fracture) in the Madhukośa commentary written by Srikanṭhadatta. 44. ＊＊＊＊

answer_text: Due to continuous consumption of foods of salty, sour and pungent tastes, and foods that are hot (in quality and potency), the dosas aggravate and cause visarpa which is of seven types. These are four - Vātika, paittika, kaphaja, sannipātaja and three caused by dual combination of three doṣa, i.e, one agneya or agnivisarpa caused by vātapitta, one granthi visarpa caused by kapha-vāta and one kardamaka caused by pitta-kapha which is very severe. 1-3. (Ca. Ci. 21)
